Ti. 59c ; τὸ ἱερὸν πεπαλαιῶσθαι Sammelb. 5827.11 (i BC) ; πεπαλαιωμένον ἔκπτωμα βραχίονος one which is of long standing, Hp. Art. 7 ; γένος παλαιωθὲν ὑπὸ χρόνου DH. 3.10 ; πεπαλαιωμένε ἡμερῶν κακῶν LXX Su. 52 ; of wine, become old, Thphr. CP 6.7.5, Gal. 14.14, al., Ath. 1.33a.
abrogate, cancel, [διαθήκην] Ep. Hebr. l.c.
ον, = παλαιόπλουτος, Ph. 1.233.
ον, = παλαιπλούσιος, Quarterly of Dept. of Ant. in Palestine 1.155 (Gaza, iii AD).
εως, ἡ, contest, Ptol. Harm. 1.1.

ατος, τό, bout or fall in wrestling, παρὰ ἓν π. ἔδραμε νικᾶν Hdt. 9.33 ; ἓν μὲν τόδ’ ἤδη τῶν τριῶν π. A. Eu. 589, cf. Pl. Phdr. 256b ; in pl., feats of wrestling, Pi. O. 9.13, P. 8.35, cf. CR 43.210 (Asia Minor).
struggle, A. Ag. 63 (anap.), Eu. 776, S. OT 880 (lyr.), E. Med. 1214 ; of war, Jul. Or. 2.66c ; παλαίσμαθ’ ἡμῶν ὁ βίος E. Supp. 550.
trick, ΄chip’ in wrestling, metaph, Ar. Ra. 689, cf. 878 ; π. δικαστηρίου a trick of the courts, Aeschin. 3.205 ; σόφισμα… καὶ π. τῶν ἀκουόντων DH. Th. 8.12 ; ὦ Θετταλὸν π., addressed to a person, Ath. 7.308b. in pl., of works of art, groups of wrestlers, Philostr. Im. 2.32.
ἡ, poet. for πάλη, the wrestler΄s art, Il. 23.701, Od. 8.103, 126, Simon. 149, Inscr.Prien. 268c2 (ii/i BC) ; παλαιμοσύνη, Aristarch. ap. Eust. 1587.40, v.l. in Tyrt. 12.2.
Aeol. for παλαιστή.
οἶνος wine that has become oily from age, Nic. Th. 591.
v. παλαίω II.
thrust away with the hand, Ps.-Luc. Philopatr. 1, Eust. 1415.21 ; cf. παλαιστή.
ἡ, = παλαστή ; Aeol. παλαίστα Alc. 33.6 (v.l. παλάσταν).
v. παλαστή.

οῦ, ὁ, (< παλαίω) wrestler, Od. 8.246, Hdt. 3.137, Pl. Lg. 819b, Trag.Adesp. 383.3, etc. ; ἄνδρες π. Ar. Lys. 1083 ; παῖδες π. CIG 1969 (Thessalonica) ; σὺν σάκει… π., of soldiers, S. Fr. 859 (lyr.). generally, rival, adversary, τοῖον π. νῦν παρασκευάζεται ἐπ’ αὐτὸς αὑτῷ A. Pr. 920 ; σοφὸς π. κεῖνος, of Odysseus, S. Ph. 431 ; λόχος… ἐξηνδρωμένος δεινὸς π. ἦν E. Supp. 704.
suitor, A. Ag. 1206.
α, ον, = παλαστιαῖος, Thphr. HP 2.7.7, Plb. 6.23.3, J. AJ 8.3.5, Heliod. ap. Orib. 49.7.1, S.E. M. 9.300, etc.

ή, όν, (< παλαίω) expert in wrestling, Arist. Rh. 1361b24, Luc. DDeor. 20.14, etc. ; ἡ παλαιστική (sc. τέχνη) the art of wrestling, Paus. 1.39.3, etc. Adv. -κῶς Poll. 3.149 ; Comp. -ώτερον Philostr. Gym. 35.
suited for wrestling, ἰσχύς Plu. 2.130b ; στέρνα παλαιστικώτερα Philostr. Gym. 35 ; cf. παλαιστρικός.
ὁ, = παλαιστή, IGRom. 1.1290 (Elephantine).

ἡ, (< παλαίω) wrestling-school, δρόμον καὶ π. ποιησάμενος Hdt. 6.126, cf. Hp. Art. 4 ; in pl., E. El. 528, Ar. Ra. 729, etc. ; εἰς παλαίστραν φοιτῆσαι Pl. Grg. 456d ; πέμπουσιν εἰς διδασκάλων μαθησομένους καὶ γράμματα καὶ μουσικὴν καὶ τὰ ἐν παλαίστρᾳ X. Lac. 2.1. Κερκυόνος π., of the spot where Cercyon slew his victims, B. 17.26, Paus. 1.39.3. metaph, school, ἡ Ἀλεξάνδρου π. Plu. Demetr. 5 ; ἡ Σωκράτους π. Longin. 4.4.
ου, ὁ, veteran, IGRom. 1.1489 (Moesia), 3.213 (Ancyra).
α, ον, suited for a παλαίστρα, αὐλίδιον Thphr. Char. 5.9.
τό, Dim. of παλαίστρα, PSI 4.418 (iii AD), cj. in Thphr. Char. 5.9.

ή, όν, of or for the wrestling-school, Alex. 325 ; ἐπιστήμη Arist. Cat. 10b4. Adv. -κῶς after the manner of the palaestra, Sch. Ar. V. 1206. later confounded with παλαιστικός, Plu. 2.639f, Sor. Fasc. 51, Gal. 6.158, Hierocl. in CA 16 p. 456M.

ου, ὁ, like a παλαιστής, athletic, Call. Fr. 191, Plu. 2.274d ; π. θεός god of the palaestra, Babr. 48.5 ; of Hermes, IG 12(5).911.22 (Tenos) ; οἱ π. those who practised in the palaestra, CIG 2627 (Cypr.) ; Medic., π. τρόπος manipulative treatment of dislocations, Heliod. ap. Orib. 49.1.1.

ακος, ὁ, superintendent of a wrestling-school, Hp. Epid. 6.8.30, IG 5(2).47 (Tegea), Inscr.Délos 372 A 98 (200 BC), OGI 345.22 (Delph., i BC), Epigr.Gr. 411, Ael. VH 8.14 ; π. τοῦ μεγάλου γυμνασίου PRyl. 121.3 (ii AD).
ατος, τό, = παλαιστή, Aq. 3Ki. 7.9 (46).
παλαίτατος, v. παλαιός.
η, ον, = παλαίφατος, ἄγνος Call. Fr. anon. 102.

ον, (< φημί) poet. Adj. spoken long ago, ἦ μάλα δή με π. θέσφαθ’ ἱκάνει Od. 9.507, cf. Pi. O. 2.40, S. OC 454 ; π. λόγος, ἀραί, A. Ag. 750 (lyr.), Th. 766 (lyr.).
spoken of long ago, legendary, δρῦς π. an oak of ancient story, Od. 19.163 (vv. ll. παλαίφαγος, παλαίφυτος, cf. Hsch.).
of ancient fame, made known or declared of old, γενεά Pi. N. 6.31 ; γένος A. Supp. 532 (lyr.) ; πρόνοια S. Tr. 823 (lyr.) ; Δίκη Id. OC 1381 ; Ἀχάρναι δὲ παλαίφατον εὐάνορες Acharnae was brave of old time, Pi. N. 2.16.
ονος, ὁ, ἡ, that has been long in a country, an ancient inhabitant, indigenous, Ἄρης A. Th. 104 (lyr.) ; δῆμος Epigr. ap. Aeschin. 3.190.

Aeol. πάλαιμι Hdn. Gr. 2.930 ; Boeot. παλήω ib. 949 ; fut. παλαίσω ; aor. ἐπάλαισα ; (πάλη¹) : — wrestle, οὐ γὰρ πύξ γε μαχήσεαι οὐδὲ παλαίσεις Il. 23.621 ; καί νύ κε τὸ τρίτον… πάλαιον ib. 733 ; παλαίουσ’ ἐς τρίς S. Fr. 941.13 ; οἱ ἐπιστάμενοι παλαίειν Pl. Prt. 350e ; ἐπάλαισαν κάλλιστα Ἀθηναίων Id. Men. 94c ; τὸν παλαίσαντά ποτ’ ἐκεῖνον him once famous as a wrestler, D. 21.71. π. τινί wrestle with one, Φιλομηλείδῃ ἐπάλαισεν Od. 4.343, 17.134 ; λέοντι Pi. P. 9.27 ; metaph, wrestle with a calamity, ἀάτῃσι Hes. Op. 413 ; φόνῳ Pi. N. 8.27 ; κακῷ μερμέρῳ E. Rh. 509 ; πολλαῖς ζημίαις X. Oec. 17.2. c. acc., overcome, λόγον λόγῳ παλαιστέον An.Ox. 3.216 ; — Pass., παλαισθείς beaten, E. El. 686 ; οἶνος… παλαίεσθαι βαρύς Id. Cyc. 678. c. inf., endeavour, Ach.Tat. 3.1.
ατος, τό, antiquity, in pl., LXX Jb. 36.28, al.

εως, ἡ, (< παλαιόομαι) keeping for a long time, esp. of wine, παλαίωσιν δέχεσθαι Str. 5.44.3, cf. Plu. 2.656b, Ath. 1.33b, Xenocr. ap. Orib. 2.58.140 ; of drugs, maturing, Hp. Decent. 10 ; dilapidated condition of a house, Stud.Pal. 22.131.7 (ii AD) ; metaph, διελθεῖν εἰς π. LXX Na. 1.15 (2.1) ; μῆνις ὀργὴ εἰς π. ἀποτιθεμένη Andronic. Rhod. p. 572 M.

fut. -ήσομαι, Aeol. -άσομαι Alc. 72 ; (< παλάμη) : — manage, execute, ταῖς χερσὶ τὸ δέον π. X. Cyr. 4.3.17.
manage adroitly, πρὸς ταῦτα Κλέων παλαμάσθω Ar. Ach. 659, cf. Nu. 176, E. Fr. 918 (lyr.) ; τόλμημα παλαμήσασθαι plan a daring deed, Ar. Pax 94 ; μηχανάς Philostr. VA 2.33. — Act. only in aor. part. παλαμήσας· τεχνάσας, Hsch.

ὁ, voc. ες Ar. Ra. 1451 ; gen. ους E. Or. 433, etc. ; dat. ει Pl. Ap. 41b, εϊ QS. 5.198 ; acc. η Pl. Ep. 311b, εα E. IA 198 (lyr.) ; but some forms occur of 1 decl., dat. ῃ Hsch. s.v. ἄκεστρον ; acc. ην Pl. Phdr. 261d ; (< παλάμη) ; — Palamedes, i.e. the Inventor, Ar. Th. 770, Ra. 1451, Paus. 2.20.3 ; — hence Adj. Παλαμήδειος, α, ον, worthy of Palamedes, ingenious, βούλευμα Alciphr. 3.4 ; ἀβάκιον EM 666.21 ; also Παλαμηδικός, ή, όν, Π. τοὐξεύρημα Eup. 351.6.

ἡ, Ep. gen. and dat. παλάμηφι, φιν ; — poet. Noun, palm of the hand ; hence, generally, hand, esp. as used in grasping, παλάμῃ δ’ ἔχε χάλκεον ἔγχος Od. 1.104 ; ἔγχος ὅ οἱ παλάμηφιν ἀρήρει Il. 3.338, cf. 1.238, etc. ; παλάμᾳ δονέων Pi. P. 1.44.
hand as used in deeds of violence, ἔπασχον ὑπ’ Ἄρηος παλαμάων by the hands of Ares, Il. 3.128, cf. 5.558, A. Supp. 865 (lyr.) ; Κυπρογενήας παλάμαισιν Alc. 60 ; hence, a deed of force, ῥέξαι παλάμαν S. Ph. 1206 (lyr.).
hand as used in works of art, etc., Il. 15.411, Hes. Th. 580, Sc. 219, 320 ; ἐργατίναις π. IG 12(2).129 (Mytil.). metaph, cunning, art, device, either in good or bad sense, π. βιότου a device for one΄s livelihood, Thgn. 624, cf. Hdt. 8.19 ; esp. of the gods, θεοῦ σὺν παλάμᾳ, θεῶν παλάμαι, παλάμαις Διός, by their arts, Pi. O. 10 (11).21, P. 1.48, N. 10.65 ; ὦ παλάμαι θεῶν S. Ph. 177 (lyr.) ; πυκνότατος παλάμαις, of Sisyphus, Pi. O. 13.52, cf. A. Pr. 167 (lyr.), etc. ; παντοίας πλέκειν παλάμας Ar. V. 645.
piece of handiwork, work of art, Hsch. (pl.) ; πυριγενὴς π., i.e. a sword, E. Or. 820 (lyr.). (Cf. Lat. palma, OE. folm ΄hand΄.)
ατος, τό, device, scheme, Com.Adesp. 706, Ael. NA 1.32.
or παλάμηφιν, Ep. gen. and dat. of παλάμη.
ίδος, ἡ, = ἀσπάλαξ, Alex.Trall. 12. = πηλαμύς, Cyran. 22.
τεχνίτης παρὰ τοῖς Σαλαμινίοις, Hsch.

ὁ, (παλάμη I. 2) one guilty of violence ; hence, murderer, τινος S. Tr. 1207 ; one defiled by blood-guiltiness, A. Eu. 448, S. El. 587, Hyp. Fr. 85 ; ὦ παλαμναίη O miscreant!, of the fox, Babr. 82.6. as Adj., τῷ π. ξένῳ the abominable stranger, Phryn.Com. 58 ; ἱκεσίαι a murderer΄s supplications, ARh. 4.709 ; ἀσπίς Orph. L. 512 ; π. μόρον ἕξει a miscreant΄s death, prob. in Supp.Epigr. 1.442 (Lydia). = ἀλάστωρ, avenger of blood, μὴ παλαμναῖον λάβω E. IT 1218, cf. X. Cyr. 8.7.18 (pl.) ; in full, δαίμονες π. avenging deities, Ti.Locr. 105, cf. Plu. Oth. 1, Jul. Caes. 336b ; Ζεὺς π. Arist. Mu. 401a23, cf. Plb. Fr. 98, Poll. 5.131, EM 647.43.
εως, ἡ, laying on of a preliminary coat of paint, priming, IG4²(1).109 iii 111, 117 (Epid., iii BC).
Aeol. for παλαιός.
τό, = παλάθιον, Ar. Pax 574 codd. (lyr. ; παλάθιον Suid.).

pf. Pass. πεπάλαγμαι, Ep. Verb, besprinkle, defile, αἵματί τ’ ἐγκεφάλῳ τε παλαξέμεν… οὖδας Od. 13.395 ; — mostly in Pass., παλάσσετο δ’ αἵματι θώρηξ Il. 5.100 ; αἵματι καὶ λύθρῳ πεπαλαγμένον Od. 22.402, cf. Call. Lav. Pall. 7 ; πεπάλακτο πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ὕπερθεν Od. 22.406 ; αἰδοῖα γονῇ πεπαλαγμένος Hes. Op. 733 ; νιφετῷ π. ὕδωρ QS. 12.410 ; — in Med., παλάσσετο χεῖρας he bespattered his hands, Il. 11.169. Pass., to be scattered abroad, ἐγκέφαλος πεπάλακτο ib. 98, 12.186. Ἀσωπὸς… πεπάλακτο κεραυνῷ was smitten, for ἐπέπληκτο, Call. Del. 78. in pf. Med., shake, i.e. draw lots from an urn, κλήρῳ νῦν πεπάλαχθε διαμπερές determine your fate by lot, Il. 7.171 ; τοὺς ἄλλους κλήρῳ πεπαλάχθάχθαι ἄνωγον Od. 9.331 ; πεπάλαχθε κατὰ κληῗδας ἐρετμά ARh. 1.358. — Aristarch. read πεπάλασθε, πεπαλάσθαι in Hom. (cf. πάλλω).

ἡ, = παλάμη, palm of the hand ; hence, as a measure of length, palm, four fingers’ breadth, IG1². 372.35, Cratin. 133, IG2². 1665.10, 1666 A 67, 70, al. (iv BC), 11 (2).287 A 95 (Delos, iii BC), CIG 2860.14 (Delos), cf. Phryn. 264, PLit. Lond. 183 ; — also παλαιστή, Hp. Nat. Mul. 33, Arist. HA 606a14, PCair. Zen. 484.11 (iii BC), Plb. 1.22.4, Hero Aut. 3.1, Geom. 4.1, DS. 1.55, etc. ; also παλαιστής, οῦ, ὁ, LXX Ex. 25.23 (25), 3Ki. 7.24, Hero Def. 131, Geom. 4.10, S.E. M. 9.300 ; written παλεστής, POxy. 669.27, 34 (iii AD) ; cf. παλαιστιαῖος.
α, ον, a palm long, broad, or high, ὕψος π. Hdt. 1.50, cf. IG2². 1675.13, 1693, 2492.44 ; later παλαιστιαῖος.
η, ον, Palatine, DH. 2.70.
τό, = Lat. Palatium, the Palatine Hill, DH. 1.31, etc.
ἡ, (παλάσσω III) anything acquired by lot, = ἀρχή, λῆξις, μοῖρα, γενεά, Hsch. ; ἐκ παλαχῆς, = ἐξ ἀρχῆς, Nic. Th. 449 (cf. Sch. ad loc.).
ἐκ γενεᾶς, ἐκ παλαιοῦ, Hsch.
ατος, τό, (παλεός = παλαιός) ancient object of hate, Tim. Pers. 90.
ον, where nymphs were born of old, ἄντρον Tim. Pers. 120 (-φαιο- Pap.).
Lacon. for παλαιός.
ατος, τό, allurement, Anon. ap. Bast. ad Greg.Cor. p. 1017S.
τὰ λίνα οἷς τὰ θηρία ἁλίσκεται, Phot.
οῦ, ὁ, decoy-bird, Hsch.
θηρευτικόν, Hsch. (πατ- cod.).
ἡ, fem. of παλευτής, Arist. HA 613a23 ; as Adj., πελειάδες Ael. NA 13.17 ; metaph, of courtesans, φιλῳδοὶ κερμάτων π. Eub. 84.1 ; — also παλευτρίς, ίδος, ἡ, Phot.
ίδος, ἡ, Phot. = παλεύτρια.

act as decoy-birds, Ar. Av. 1083, 1087 ; — Pass., of a bird, to be decoyed, Philostr. Im. 2.33. metaph, π. τινά decoy, entrap, Plu. 2.52b, Sull. 28, etc. ; π. τινὰ τοῖς ἀφροδισίοις Philostr. VA 4.25 ; abs., Ph. 1.654.

to be disabled, εἰ παλήσειε ὁ ναυτικὸς στρατός Hdt. 8.21 ; elsewh. only in Hsch., παλήσειε· διαφθαρείη. ἐπάλησεν· ἐφθάρη. πεπαληκέναι· ἐκπεσεῖν. πεπαλημέναι· βεβλαμμέναι ; also in shortd. forms, πεπαλμένος· βεβλαμμένος, Id., Phot. ; πεπαλκέναι λέγεται τὸ ἐκπίπτειν τὰ πλοῖα Id.

(or παλή acc. to Sch. Il. 10.7, to dist. it from πάλη¹), ἡ, the finest meal, π. ἀλφίτου Hp. Mul. 1.64, cf. Ruf. Ren. Ves. 6.7, Arching. ap. Gal. 12.791 ; π. πυρίνη Lycus ap. Orib. 9.51.1 ; νάρθηκος πάλαι Zopyr. ap. eund. 14.61.1.
any fine dust, ἀνέπλησα τὠφθαλμὼ πάλης φυσῶν τὸ πῦρ Pherecr. 60, cf. Hsch. (Cf. Lat. pollen, pulvis.)

ἡ, wrestling, Il. 23.635 ; ἢ πὺξ ἠὲ πάλῃ ἢ καὶ ποσίν Od. 8.206 ; κρατέων πάλα Pi. O. 8.20 ; νικᾶν πυγμὴν καὶ π. E. Alc. 1031. cf. Hp. Acut. (Sp.) 62, Th. 1.6, Pl. Lg. 795b, Plu. 2.638d, Antyll. ap. Orib. 6.28.3 ; τίνα π. ἐμάνθανες ; Ar. Eq. 1238 ; παίδων, ἐφήβων νεωτέρων, μέσων, πρεσβυτέρων, ἀνδρῶν π., SIG 959 (Chios), cf. IG 5(2).549.16, 30 (Lycosura, iv BC), etc. generally, fight, battle, ἅπτειν πάλην τινί A. Ch. 866 (anap.) ; π. δορός E. Heracl. 159.
ατος, τό, = πάλη², π. ὀρόβοιο Nic. Al. 551.
τό, Dim. of πάλημα, Ar. Fr. 682.
Boeot. for παλαιός.
Boeot. for παλαίω.

later poet. form of πάλιν, Call. Epigr. 12, AP 5.181 (Mel.), Epigr.Gr. 314 (Smyrna), Orph. H. 3.10, Scymn. 470 ; also in later Prose, Phld. Mus. pp. 17, 40 K., Anon. Lond. 6.36, 18.4, POxy. 298.27 (i AD), cf. Phryn. 249.
ωτος, ὁ, mutual mockery, prob. l. in Ph. 1.528.

ἡ, rebirth, regeneration, of the world, παλιγγενεσίας ἡγεμόνες, of Noah and his sons, Id. 2.144 ; ἡ ἀνάκτησις καὶ π. τῆς πατρίδος J. AJ 11.3.9 ; renewal of a race, Corp.Herm. 3.3 ; of persons, beginning of a new life, εἰς π. ὁρμᾶν Ph. 1.159, cf. Luc. Musc. Enc. 7 ; hence of restoration after exile, Cic. Att. 6.6.4 ; transmigration, reincarnation of souls, Plu. 2.998c ; cf. μετεμψύχωσις fin. in Stoic Philos., rebirth of the κόσμος, Chrysipp. Stoic. 2.191 ; pl., ib. 187, Boeth. Stoic. 3.265 ; so later, ἡ περιοδικὴ π. τῶν ὅλων M.Ant 11.1, cf. Procl. in Ti. 3.241 D.
Medic., relapse, Gal. 13.83 ; regrowth of a tumour, Antyll. ap. Orib. 45.2.7.
in Roman Law, = restitutio natalium, Just. Nov. 18.11.
in NT., resurrection, Ev. Matt. 19.28.
regeneration by baptism, διὰ λουτροῦ παλιγγενεσίας Ep. Tit. 3.5.
ές, born again, Nonn. D. 2.650 ; generated anew, αἰών PMagLond. 121.510.

ον, contradictory, false, ἀγγέλων ῥῆσις Pi. N. 1.58 ; but ἔρις οὐ π. unrelenting, Id. Parth. 2.63.
of strange or foreign tongue, πόλις Id. I. 6 (5).24. = δύσφημος, Com.Adesp. 1098.
ον, bent or doubled back, κέλευθοι Tryph. 523 ; written παλίγναμπτος in Opp. C. 2.305, H. 1.54.
gloss on παλινδαές, Hsch.
ἡ, revision of a γραφή III, Jul. Laod. in Cat.Cod.Astr. 5(1).191.
to be a retail dealer, D. 56.7.
ὁ, retailer of imported produce, Ar. Pl. 1156 (ὁ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐμπόρου ἀγοράζων καὶ πωλῶν Sch.) ; metaph, π. πονηρίας D. 25.46.
σκολιόν, αὐστηρόν, δύστροπον, Hsch.
ές, bent back, gloss on παλιμπετές, Sch. ARh. 4.1315.
= παλιγκοτέω, Hp. Fract. 11, Mul. 2.171.
of wounds, grow malignant, fester, Hp. Fract. 11, 25.
εως, ἡ, festering, of a wound, Hp. Fract. 31 (pl.).
ἡ, = παλιγκότησις, Hp. Art. 67 (pl.).

ον, spiteful, malignant, resentful, ἀλλά τις οὐκ ἔμμι παλιγκότων ὄργαν Sappho 72 ; κληδόνες π. injurious, untoward reports, A. Ag. 863, 874 ; π. τύχη the spitefulness of fortune, ib. 571 ; πῆμα Pi. O. 2.20 ; π. ὄψιν ἰδοῦσα a dreadful sight, Mosch. 4.92 ; τὰ π. λέγειν Antipho Soph. 49. of persons, hostile, malignant, τινι Ar. Pax 390, Euph. 51.12, etc. ; πρὸς πάντα π. Theoc. 22.58 ; οἱ παλίγκοτοι adversaries, Pi. N. 4.96, A. Supp. 376. Adv., αὐτῷ… τως συνεφέρετο it fared ill with him, Hdt. 4.156 ; φέρειν τὰ συμπίπτοντα μὴ π. to bear accidents not resentfully, E. Fr. 572.2. metaph, of wounds or injuries, growing malignant, festering, Hp. Art. 27 (Sup.).
steep, rugged, πάγος τρηχύς τε καὶ π. Archil. 87. (Cf. ἀλλόκοτος).
ἡ, revision of a κρίσις II.1, Jul. Laod. in Cat.Cod.Astr. 5(1).191 (prob.).
εως, ἡ, recovery of possession, Rhetor. in Cat.Cod.Astr. 7.196 (pl.).
redivivus, Gloss.
ὁ, fishing-net, Plb. Fr. 65.
ον, looking back, cj. in Alcm. 145.
σφαιρίζειν, Hsch. (fort. παλλ-).
ές, gloss on παλιμπετές (fort. παλιγκαμπής), Sch. Par. ARh. 4.1315.

οἱ, a lake near Leontini in Sicily, emitting two jets of volcanic gas, Arist. Mir. 834b8, Str. 6.2.9, DS. 11.88.
in Mythol., sons of Zeus, worshipped at Palice, A. Fr. 6, DS. l.c.
gloss on παλινάγρετος, Hsch.
repeat, recapitulate, ὥς οἱ ἐπαλιλλόγητο [τὸ πρῆγμα] Hdt. 1.118, cf. 90, Arist. Rh. Al. 1433b31, Phld. Po. 5.26, Ph. 2.358, J. AJ 17.5.5, App. Mith. 14, Simp. in Ph. 1159.4.

ἡ, recapitulation, Arist. Rh. Al. 1433b29 ; pl., ib. 1428a8.
equivocation, Thphr. Char. 1.7 (pl.).
ον, (λέγω²) collected again, Il. 1.126.
ον, loosed again, unloosed, Nonn. D. 35.250, al.
ὁ, a reversed βακχειος, Heph. 3.2, Aristid.Quint. 1.22, Eust. 1551.54 ; — hence Adj. παλιμβακχειακός, ή, όν, Heph. 13.1.
ές, = ὕπτιος, Call. Fr. anon. 52.
ον, (< βαίνω) walking back, ἱστῶν παλίμβαμοι ὁδοί, of women working at the loom, since they had to walk to and fro from side to side, Pi. P. 9.18.
ον, living again, Keil-Premerstein Erster Bericht p. 9, Hsch., Phot., Suid.
ές, sprouting or growing again, κύων, of the hydra, E. HF 1274 ; καυλοί Thphr. HP 7.2.4.
εῖσα, έν, ricochetting, βέλος Ruf. Interrog. 60.
ἡ, change of mind, fickleness, AP 5.301.12 (Agath.), Agath. 2.6.

ον, reversed, γνώμη Sch. Ar. Nu. 298 ; hence, untrustworthy, unstable, ἤθη π. καὶ ἄπιστα Pl. Lg. 705a, cf. D.Chr. 31.37, Aristaenet. 1.28 ; δολερὸς καὶ π. Plu. Crass. 21 ; τὸ π., = παλιμβολία, Aeschin. 2.40 ; of a slave, = παλίμπρατος, Men. 445 ; πέδιλα π. turned or patched sandals, Nic. Fr. 85. Adv. -λως Poll. 3.132.
ου, ὁ, a wind counter to the prevalent north wind, Thphr. Vent. 28 (pl.).
f.l. for παλιμβολία, Adam. 2.24.
f.l. for παλιμβολος, Adam. 1.15, Sch. Th. 3.37, Eust. 375.1.
renew the fight, Lyd. Mag. 3.55.
ἡ, repeated change, εἰς σώματα Plu. 2.998d.
ες, as long again, doubly long, χρόνος A. Ag. 196 (lyr.).
παιδος, ὁ, ἡ, again a child, Luc. Sat. 9.
ον, dub.l., epith. of πέλαγος, Dion.Byz. 53.
ἡ, recurrence, Theol.Ar. 58.

ές, (< πίπτω) falling back, Nonn. D. 3.30 ; recurrent, Theol.Ar. 57 ; in early writers only in neut. as Adv., back again, ἂψ ἐπὶ νῆας ἔεργε παλιμπετές Il. 16.395 ; ὡς… ἐν νηῒ παλιμπετὲς ἀπονέωνται Od. 5.27, cf. Call. Del. 294, ARh. 2.1250, etc.
τά, (< πήγνυμι) cobbled shoes, Com.Adesp. 1099.
εως, ἡ, patching up or cobbling of shoes, Thphr. Char. 22.11.
ἡ, pitch reboiled, dry pitch, Dsc. 1.72 ; cf. παλίνπιττα.
ον, back-driven, δρόμοι A. Pr. 838.
Pass., only in aor. part. παλιμπλαγχθείς, foiled, driven back, Il. 1.59, Od. 13.5 (better divisim).
ές, wandering to and fro, Μαίανδρος AP 6.287 (Antip., v.l. πολυ-)· βίοτος Epigr.Gr. 491.5 (Orchom. Boeot.).
ές, twined or plaited back, κύρτοι Oppian. H. 4.47.
ὁ, ἡ, πλουν, τό, sailing back, Ael. NA 3.14.
ον, washed up again, vamped up ; metaph, of a plagiarist who retouches the works of others and passes them off for his own, κηφὴν π. AP 7.708 (Diosc.).
ον, Ion. for παλίμπλους, Lyc. 1431.
ἡ, counter-wind, Thphr. Vent. 26 ; poet. παλιμπνοίη ARh. 1.586 (pl.).
η, ον, poet. as παλίμπνοος, eddying, δῖναι cj. in Oppian. H. 1.771.
ον, breathing again, Nonn. D. 37.295 ; poet. παλίμπνοιος, η, ον, eddying, δῖναι cj. in Oppian. H. 1.771.

ον, retributive, δίκαι Max. 17.
παλίμποινα, τά, retribution, repayment, A. Ch. 793 (lyr.).
ον, = παλίμπορος, Tim. Pers. 186, Lyc. 180, 628.
ον, going back, φυγή Tim. Pers. 174, cf. Oppian. H. 4.529, Nonn. D. 2.247.
ου, ὁ, = παλίμποτον, Inscr.Délos 442 B 205 (ii BC, pl.).
τό, reversible cup, Michel 39.37, 40 (Milet., iii BC) ; — also παλιμπότης, ου, ὁ, Inscr.Délos 442 B 205 (ii BC, pl.).
ὁ, ἡ, gen. ποδος, going back, returning, Lyc. 126, AP 5.162 (Mel.) ; π. ἡ τύχη περιΐσταται J. BJ 4.1.6.
to be a retailer, PRev. Laws 47.16 (iii BC).
ου, ὁ, = παλιγκάπηλος, Socr. Ep. 1.1.
ον, sold again or by retail, of a good-for-nothing slave who passes from hand to hand, Poll. 3.125. generally, good-for-nothing, Ph. 2.523, Poll. 4.36 ; also of things, D.Chr. 31.37, Poll. 7.12.
ἡ, double treachery, Plb. 5.96.4, DH. 8.32, DS. 15.91, etc.
ου, ὁ, traitor to both sides, Din. Fr. 89.26, DS. 15.91, App. BC 5.96.
Adv. stern-foremost, E. IT 1395, from Hsch., who expl. it οἷον παλίμπρυμνον χώρησιν.
Adv. rump-foremost, Arist. PA 659a20, Hsch.
ον, = παλίμπρατος, v.l. in Poll. 7.12 ; esp. of works not completed by the first contractor and given to another, IG 7.3073.26 (Lebad.), BCH 20.324 (ibid.).
Dor. for παλίμφημος.

Dor. παλίμφαμος, ον, back-speaking, recanting, π. ἀοιδά, = παλινῳδία, a song of recantation, reproaching the male sex instead of the female, E. Ion 1096 (lyr.), cf. Med. 415 sq. = κακόφημος, δύσφημος, λαβροσύναι Tryph. 423, cf. Hsch. ; π. εὐχαί Ph. 2.301 ; ὄναρ ib. 55.
ον, returning, Max. 332, 570, PMich. in Class.Phil. 22.16.
ονος, ὁ, ἡ, changing one΄s mind, Lyc. 1349.
ές, growing again, of the hydra, Luc. Am. 2.

deleticia (sc.
charta), Gloss.
ον, (< ψάω) scraped again, βιβλίον π. palimpsest, Plu. 2.779c ; -ψηστον, τό, as Subst., ib. 504d, cf. Catull. 22.5, Cic. Fam. 7.18.2.

poet. also πάλι, Adv. of Place, back, backwards (the usual sense in early Ep.), mostly joined with Verbs of going, coming, etc. ; π. χώρει Hdt. 5.72 ; π. ἐλεύσεται, κατελθεῖν, ἐπανέλθωμεν, A. Pr. 854, S. OC 601, Pl. Cra. 438a, etc. ; κέλευθον ἥνπερ ἦλθες ἐγκόνει π. A. Pr. 962 ; δίκα καὶ πάντα π. στρέφεται E. Med. 412 (lyr.) ; δεῦρο σωθήσῃ π. Id. Ph. 725, cf. 1400 ; δόμεναι π. give back, restore, Il. 1.116, etc. ; π. ἀποδοῦναι And. 2.23 ; π. ἀγκαλέσαι to call back, A. Ag. 1021 (lyr.) ; less freq. c. gen., π. τράπεθ’ υἷος ἑοῖο she turned back from her son, Il. 18.138 ; δόρυ Ἀχιλλῆος π. ἔτραπεν 20.439, cf. Od. 7.143 ; coupled with other Advbs., π. αὖτις ἔβαινον νηὸς ἐπὶ γλαφυρῆς 14.356, cf. Pi. O. 1.65 ; αὖ π. Od. 13.125 ; ἂψ π. Il. 18.280 ; π. εἶσιν ὀπίσσω Od. 11.149 ; π. φέρεσθαι ἐξοπίσω Hes. Th. 181 ; ἄψορρον π. S. El. 53 ; π. οἴκαδε, π. οἴκαδ’ αὖ, Ar. Lys. 792, Ra. 1486 ; π. αὖ Pl. Prt. 318e, etc. ; with the Art., ἡ π. ὁδός E. Or. 125. to express contradiction, π. ἐρέει gainsay, Il. 9.56 ; π. ὅ γε λάζετο μῦθον took back his word, unsaid it, 4.357 ; opp. ἀληθέα εἰπεῖν, Od. 13.254 ; μηδέ τῳ δόξῃ π. let no one think contrariwise, A. Th. 1045 ; in Prose, contrariwise, Pl. Grg. 482d ; π. αὖ Id. R. 507b ; αὖ… π. Id. Ap. 27d ; in this sense sts. c. gen., τὸ π. νεότατος youth΄s opposite, Pi. O. 10 (11).87 ; χρόνου τὸ π. the change of time, E. HF 777 (lyr.) ; cf. ἔμπαλιν. of Time, again, once more, rare in Hom., Il. 2.276, cf. S. OT 1166, X. Mem. 1.6.11, etc. ; freq. coupled with αὖ, αὖθις ; π. ἐξ ἀρχῆς Ar. Pax 997, etc. ; π. καὶ π. Str. 17.1.3, Plu. 2.565d, Ael. VH 1.4 ; ἔγχει καὶ π. εἰπέ, π. π. "Ἡλιοδώρας" AP 5.135 (Mel.) ; both senses (I and II) are appropriate in Od. 16.456, Pl. Prt. 322b, etc.
in turn, S. El. 371, Ar. Ach. 342, Call. Dian. 87, etc. ; π. ὁ κῦρος ἠρώτα X. An. 1.6.7 ; π. ἀπαιτῶ Pl. R. 612d ; again, πρῶτον μέν… ἔπειτα π. Arist. Pol. 1289b29, etc. (In compos. πάλιν sts. means doubly, as in παλιμμήκης, παλίνσκιος.)
ον, bringing messages to and fro, Hsch., Phot., Suid.

ον, (< ἀγρέω) to be taken back or recalled, οὐ π. οὐδ’ ἀπατηλόν irrevocable, Il. 1.526 ; π. ἀάτη Hes. Sc. 93 ; νεότατα δ’ ἔχειν π. οὐκ ἔστι Theoc. 29.28 ; π. αἰών, ἀρχή, etc., Nonn. D. 3.255, 6.175, al. ; recoverable, of an element, Numen. ap. Eus. PE 15.17.
retracting his words, of the philosopher Arcesilaus, Id. ib. 14.5.

ον, removed from office and re-elected, of public officers, Eup. 89, Archipp. 14, Nicostr. 34. of buildings, pulled down and rebuilt, patched up, Pi. Fr. 84, cf. Harp. s.v., Hsch., etc. ; also σιδήρου π. IG1². 313.131 (Eleusis). παλιναίρετα γεγονότα… καὶ διεφθαρμένα Pl. Ti. 82e, expld. by Tim. Lex. φευκτά, ἔκβλητα, τὸ ἐναντίον… αὐτῇ τῇ αἱρέσει πάθος ἐμποιοῦντα.
ές, growing again, APl. 4.221 (Theaet.), Nonn. D. 25.542.
ὁ, deserting back again, double deserter, X. HG 7.3.10.
ές, (< *δάω) learnt again, Hsch.
go to law again, bring a fresh action, BGU 613.17 (ii AD), Hsch.
ἡ, second action, new trial, π. διδόναι τινί Hdn. 7.6.4 ; π. εὑρίσκειν Plu. Dem. 6 ; μὴ ἦμεν… π. Tab.Heracl. 1.157.
ον, litigious, CratesCom. 51.
ον, whirling round and round, θάλασσα AP 9.73 (Antiphil.) ; κόσμοιο παλινδίνητον ἀνάγκην ib. 1.19 (Claudian.), cf. 9.505.14.
ἡ, eddying of water, Hsch.
εως, ἡ, = παλίωξις, App. Pun. 46, DC. 74.6.
ἡ, mending of shoes ; hence in concrete, mended shoes, Pl.Com. 164, cf. Poll. 6.164.

run back again, ἐπὶ τόπον J. BJ 3.2.3 ; ἐς ταὐτά Aret. SD 1.6 ; abs., Manetho ap. J. Ap. 1.26 ; of a ship, Ps.-Hdt. Vit. Hom. 19, DS. 20.74, Plu. Cic. 32 ; prov., παλινδρομῆσαι μᾶλλον ἢ κακῶς δραμεῖν Luc. Asin. 18.
ΙΙ. Medic., go back without coming to a head, of an abscess, dub. in Hp. Prog. 18 ; μὴ δρομῇ τὸ ἐρυσίπελας ἔσω strike inwards, ib. 23.
b. recur, relapse, Id. Epid. 2.3.18, Aret. SA 1.7, Luc. Abd. 32.
c. παλινδρομῶν σφυγμός recurrent, recovering, Gal. 9.510, Marcellin. Puls. 400.
d. of recurrent nerves, Gal. 8.53, UP 16.4.
ΙII. metaph, π. πρὸς τὰς τῶν Καρχηδονίων ἐλπίδας fall back upon…, Plb. 7.3.8 ; γεωμετρία ἐπὶ τὰ αἰσθητὰ δρομοῦσα Plu. 2.718f.
2. βλασφημία δρομοῦσα, of abuse which comes home to roost, ib. 88d.
ές, = παλίνδρομος, ἐς ταὐτά Aret. SA 2.9.
εως, ἡ, = παλινδρομία, Eust. 244.28.

Ion. -ίη, ἡ, running back, going backwards, AP 6.307 (Phan.), Iamb. in Nic. p. 76P. ; τοῦ ἡλίου DL. 7.152 ; τῆς φύσιος ἡ π. restoration, Aret. CD 1.3 ; striking inwards, of an abscess or eruption, Hp. Prorrh. 2.7 ; in pl., relapses, Id. Epid. 4.42.
ή, όν, recurring, of the tide, κίνησις Str. 1.3.8.

ον, running back again, π. ἄπιθι Luc. Tim. 37 ; recurring, σελήνη π. ἀνάμνησις Secund. Sent. 6 ; π. ἔλλαβε πένθος recurring, Epigr.Gr. 233.7 (Chios) ; μνᾶς… παλινδρόμους ἀπολαβεῖν back again, DL. 2.65 ; metaph, uncertain, S.E. P. 2.203.
ον, coming home to roost, πτηνῶν γένη π. PMagPar. 1.2556.
α, ὁ, one who squanders again, Cerc. 4.12.
ὁ, retail-dealer, Phot.
redivivus, Gloss.
ἡ, = πάλη², EM 650.3.
ἡ, returning calm, AP 10.102 (Bass. ; v.l. πολυν-).
εως, ἡ, sinking, settling down, Hp. Hum. 2.
ἡ, return of rejected blocks to a quarry, Supp.Epigr. 4.453.30 (Didyma, ii BC).
ον, returning, Nonn. D. 6.62, al.
retrace one΄s path ; hence in Math., recur, of numbers, Theol.Ar. 22.
ἡ, (< ὁδός) retracing one΄s path ; hence, recurrence of numbers, Theol.Ar. 57 (pl.) ; κατὰ παλινοδίαν ib. 59.
ἐκ δευτέρου μαντεῖαι, Hsch.
τὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἡλίου ἀπεστραμμένα, Hp. ap. Gal. 19.127.
η, ον, rushing back, Il. 11.326 (better divisim).
ον, (ὁρμάω) = παλίνορσος, Sch. Ar. Ach. 1178, Sch. S. OT 193.

ον, backwards, back, ὡς ὅτε τίς τε δράκοντα ἰδὼν παλίνορσος ἀπέστη Il. 3.33, cf. Emp. 35.1 ; ἄγε νῆα… π. ἐς Ἑλλάδα ARh. 1.416 ; π. φορή retrograde movement, Aret. SA 2.5 ; recurrent, ἣν ἡ νοῦσος π. ὀφθῇ Id. CD 1.5 ; neut. as Adv., back again, AP 7.608 (Eutolm.) ; Att. παλίνορρον, with a backward wrench, Ar. Ach. 1179. (-ορσος prob. = ὄρρος, cf. παλιμπυγηδόν.)
ον, (< ὄρνυμι) recurring, inveterate, μῆνις A. Ag. 154 (lyr.).
return, Gal. 16.89, Olymp. in Mete. 112.20.
ον, returning, ὁρμή Oppian. H. 1.616, cf. Nonn. D. 11.413.
ον, (< οὖρον) making water again, with play on pr. n. Palinurus, Mart. 3.78.2.
ἑφθὴ πίττα, Hsch. ; cf. παλίμπισσα.
v. παλιρρύμη.
χήρα γυνή, Hsch.

ον, shaded over again, thick-shaded, ἐν σκίῳ Archil. 34, Plu. Num. 10, cf. Is. Fr. 112 ; π. ἐλαῖαι Arist. HA 556a24 ; ὗλαι Luc. Am. 12 ; dark, χειμών S. Fr. 289 ; — also παλίσκιος, ον, ἄντρον h.Merc. 6, h.Hom. 18.6 ; ἐν σκίοις Thphr. HP 1.8.1, cf. Od. 40 ; εἰς τὸ π. Max.Tyr. 5.1.
ἡ, looking back again, παλινσκοπιὰν ἔχομεν E. Or. 1262 (lyr.).
ον, safe again, Nonn. D. 25.535 codd. (leg. παλίμπνοον).
return from secession, of the Roman plebs, f.l. for πάλιν ἀστατοῦντος, Lyd. Mag. 1.38.
= δυσφημέω, speak words of ill omen, A. Th. 258.
ές, reversed, βήματα S. Ichn. 112.
ον, turned backward, Κριός Max. 80, cf. Nic. Th. 679 (v.l. παλίστρ-).
ον, whirled or twirled round, Lyc. 739.
ον, = παλίνστρεπτος, Opp. C. 2.99 ; παλίστροφος, Sch. Ar. Nu. 298.
ον, gathered again, Hsch., Phot. s.v. παλίλλογα.
ον, (< τίνω) done in requital, παλίντιτα ἔργα γενέσθαι Od. 1.379. Act., requiting, πνεύματα Emp. 111.5.
ἡ, demand for repayment of interest, Plu. 2.295d.

ον, bent backward, i.e. the opposite way to that in which they were drawn, τόξα, in Hom. of the bow whether strung, Il. 8.266, cf. 15.443 ; or unstrung, 10.459, Od. 21.11, cf. S. Tr. 511 (lyr.) ; Ἀράβιοι τόξα π. εἶχον μακρά Hdt. 7.69 ; Σκυθικὰ π. βέλη A. Ch. 161 (lyr.).
back-stretched, ἡνίαι Ar. Av. 1739.
caused by opposite tensions, π. ἁρμονίη κόσμου ὅκωσπερ λύρης καὶ τόξου Heraclit. 51 (v.l. παλίντροπος). παλίντονα, τά, military engines for throwing stones, but not pointed missiles, = λιθοβόλα, Ph.Mech. Bel. 91.36, Hero Bel. 74, 104, etc.
ἡ, = παλιντροπία, Poll. 3.132.
ον, = παλίντροπος II. 2, Pi. O. 2.37.

[ᾰ,τρῐ] ές, rubbed again and again, of the ass, obstinate, resisting all blows, Semon. 7.43.
knavish, crafty, τὰ… πανοῦργα καὶ π. S. Ph. 448.
ιβος, ὁ, ἡ, = παλιντριβής, Gloss.
return, ἐπὶ νῆα τροπάασθαι ARh. 4.165 ; ἂψ δὲ τροπόωντο ib. 643.
ές, = παλίντροπος, Nic. Th. 402.
ἡ, turning about ; in pl., changes of mind, ARh. 3.1157.

ον, turned away, averted, ὄμματα, ὄψις, A. Ag. 777 (lyr.), Supp. 173 (lyr.).
turning back, π. ἕρπειν, στρέφεσθαι, S. Ph. 1222, E. HF 1069 (lyr.) ; π. ἐκ πολέμοιο AP 9.61 ; π. κέλευθος Parm. 6.9.
changing to the other side, contrary, πλάστιγξ τοῦ βίου S. Fr. 576.5 (s.v.l.) ; π. τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀποβαινούσης πρὸς τὰς ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἐπιβολάς Plb. 14.6.6 ; π. ταῖς ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἐλπίσιν exactly contrary to their original expectations, Id. 5.16.9, cf. 9.21.1 ; π. ποιῆσαι τὴν μάχην DS. 15.85, cf. App. Mith. 88 ; π. ποιήσασθαι τὴν δίωξιν Onos. 27 (v.l. παλίστροφον)· τὸ π. τοῦ δαιμονίου changeableness, Id. 35.4. Act., turning to flight, νόημα B. 10.54. v. παλίντονος 1.3.
ές, beaten back, neut. as Adv., ARh. 3.1254.
ές, with a reverse of fortune, τριβὰ βίου A. Ag. 464 (lyr.).

recant an ode ; hence, generally, revoke, recant, Pl. Alc. 2.142d, 148b ; π. πρὸς τὸ χεῖρον Luc. Apol. 1.
repeat an ode ; hence, generally, repeat, Ph. 1.586, S.E. M. 7.202.
one must recant, Gal. 11.224.

ἡ, palinode, recantation, first used of an ode by Stesichorus, in which he recanted his attack upon Helen, Isoc. 10.64, Pl. Ep. 319e, Phdr. 243b. generally, recantation, ib. 257a, Cic. Att. 4.5.1, Ph. 1.260, Plu. Alex. 53.
ή, όν, palinodic, i.e. having the form a b b a, of metrical schemes, Heph. Poëm. 4 ; π. ὕμνοι Cratin. 6 D.
ον, (< ὥρα) changing and returning with the seasons, Arat. 452. παλινώρους· ἄκοντας, Hsch. (παλίνωρον is f.l. for παλίνορρον, Id.).
[ᾱ], τό, Dor. for Πήλιον.
η, ον, made of παλίουρος, Str. 16.4.17.
= ruta, Gloss.

ὁ (Thphr. HP 1.3.2, Agatharch. 34) or ἡ (AP 9.414 (Tull. Gem.)), Christ΄s thorn, Paliurus australis, E. Cyc. 394, Theopomp.Hist. 129, Theoc. 24.89, Dsc. 1.92, etc.
great jujube, Zizyphus Spina-Christi, Thphr. HP 4.3.3, Agatharch. l.c., BGU 1120.16 (i BC), Plin. HN 13.111. = κάδος, ἀντλητήρ, Hsch.
θρῖναξ, ὁ, three-pronged fork made of the wood of the παλίουρος 1, AP 6.95 (Antiphil.).

ebb and flow, Str. 1.3.8, 3.3.3 ; ἀέρος παλιρροοῦντος Thphr. Vent. 10.
flow back, of perspiration, Diocl. Fr. 147.

η, ον, back-rushing, refluent, π. δέ μιν αὖτις πλῆξεν [τὸ κῦμα] Od. 5.430 ; ἤπειρόνδε π. φέρε κῦμα, of the wave caused by the rock thrown by the Cyclops, 9.485 ; πενίης κῦμα π. Luc. Epigr. 2.12 ; generally, = παλίρροος, ναῦς π. Arat. 347 ; τὰ π., = παλίρροια, ARh. 1.1170.
v. παλίρροχθος.

(also παλιρροία S. Fr. 832), Ion. παλιρροίη, ἡ, flowing back, backwater, δίνας τινὰς… ἰσχυρὰς καὶ παλιρροίην Hdt. 2.28 ; παλιρροία βυθοῦ, of the tide, S. l.c. ; παλιρροίῃ ἐπινήχεται, of Delos, Call. Del. 193 ; in pl., Agathem. 5.22. generally, reflux, ἡ π. τῆς ὑγρότητος, in the spleen, Arist. PA 670b8 ; τοῦ θερμοῦ Id. Insomn. 461a6 ; ἐς π. ἰέναι Aret. CA 1.7. metaph, παράδοξος π. τῶν πραγμάτων, of fortune, Plb. 1.82.3 ; ἡ ἐπ’ ἀμφότερα τὰ μέρη τῆς τύχης π. DS. 18.59 ; also of ἀνάμνησις, Ph. 1.593.
= παλίρροια.
ον, dashing back with a roar, Oppian. H. 5.220 (v.l. παλίρροιζος).
Ion. for παλίρροια.
ον, = παλίρροος, of waves, δῖναι Lyc. 380, Oppian. H. 1.778.

ον, contr. παλίρρους, ρουν, back-flowing, refluent, κλύδων E. IT 1397 ; ebbing and flowing, metaph, of the breath, ἀήρ Oppian. H. 2.398 ; ἄσθμα Tryph. 76. metaph, recurring, returning upon one΄s head, πότμος E. HF 739 (lyr.), cf. El. 1155 (lyr.).
ον, toltering, bent, π. γόνυ (of an old man) ib. 492.
ρουν, v. παλίρροος.
ον, roaring with ebb and flow, of Aulis, prob. in A. Ag. 190 (lyr., restd. metri gr. for παλιρρόθοις).
or παλινρύμη [υ], ἡ, rush backwards, back-flow, τοῦ σάλου Plu. Flam. 10 ; π. τύχης a reverse of fortune, Plb. 15.7.1, DS. 3.51 (mostly and perh. rightly written divisim in codd.).
ον, = παλίρροος, π. αἷμα flowing in retribution, prob. for πολύρρυτον in S. El. 1420 (lyr.) ; π. παγαί, of honey, dub. in Philox. 3.8 (μελιρρύτοισι Mein.).
v. παλίνσκιος.
ον, (< σύρω) dragged back, Corp.Herm. 10.8 (v.l. -συτος).
rush quickly back, of waves, DS. 1.32, 3.22.
ον, (< σεύω, ἔσσυμαι) rushing back, π. δράμημα hurried flight, S. OT 193 (lyr.) ; π. στεῖχε E. Supp. 388 ; ὁρμῆσαι Plb. 15.12.2, cf. παλίσσυρτος· χολή Aret. SD 1.15 ; π. φύσις recovering, Id. CA 2.3.
v. παλίνστρεπτος.
v. παλίνστροφος.
to be stiff-necked, refractory, contumacious, PPetr. 3 p. 136 (iii BC).

εως, ἡ, (< πάλι, ἰωκή) pursuit in turn, when fugitives rally and turn on their pursuers, π. δὲ γένηται ἐκ νηῶν [ι metri gr.] Il. 12.71 ; ἄν τοι ἔπειτα π. παρὰ νηῶν αἰὲν ἐγὼ τεύχοιμι 15.69, cf. 601 ; opp. προΐωξις, Hes. Sc. 154 ; in late Prose, App. Mith. 49.
πηλός, Hsch.
f.l. in A. Supp. 296, v. ἐμπάλαγμα.

τό, statue of Pallas, Hdt. 4.189, Ar. Ach. 547, Jahresh. 16 Beibl. 42 (iv BC), IG2². 1388.67, etc. ; Π. ἐκάλουν τὰ βαλλόμενα εἰς γῆν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀγάλματα Pherecyd. 179 J. a court of the ἐφέται at Athens, ἐπὶ Π. δώσεις δίκην Ar. Fr. 585, cf. Arist. Ath. 57.3, Paus. 1.28.8 sq.
ἡ, ball (σφαῖρα ἐκ ποικίλων ναμάτων (fort. νημάτων) πεποιημένη Hsch.), read by Dionysodorus for σφαῖρα in Od. 6.115.
or παλλακία, ἡ, concubinage, Is. 3.39 (παλλακίδι codd.), Str. 17.1.46, Peripl. M.Rubr. 49.

to be a concubine, esp. for ritual purposes, Str. 17.1.46, BCH 7.276 (Tralles) ; generally, τῷ Μιθριδάτῃ Str. 13.4.3 ; — more freq. in Med. and Pass., keep as a concubine, Hdt. 4.155. Pass., to be a concubine, Plu. Them. 26 ; τινι to one, Id. Fab. 21, Art. 26.

ἡ, = παλλακίς, πολλὰς κουριδίας γυναῖκας, πολλῷ δὲ πλεῦνας παλλακάς Hdt. 1.135, cf. 84, 2.130, al., Ar. V. 1353, Antipho 1.14, Lex ap. D. 23.53, Lys. 1.31, Pl. Ion 538b, Lg. 841d, D. 59.122, LXX Jd. 19.1, etc. ; μηδὲ π. μηδὲ παιδικὸν ἔχειν Mitteis Chr. 284.4 (ii BC). (Prop.
young girl, Ael. Dion. Fr. 172 ; cf. πάλλαξ.)
= παλλακεία.
τό, Dim. of παλλακίς, Plu. 2.789b.
ὁ, son by a concubine, Sophr. 124.
τό, Dim. of πάλλαξ, Alcm. 92 (dub.l.), Pl.Com. 206, Ael. Dion. Fr. 172 (who rejects the form παλλήκιον), Hsch. = παλλακεία, Gloss.

ίδος, ἡ, concubine, opp. lawful wife (ἄκοιτις), Il. 9.449, 452 ; ὠνητὴ π. Od. 14.203, cf. LXX Jb. 19.17, Heroph. ap. Sor. 2.53 (dub.l.), etc. ; π. δούλη AP 3.3 (Inscr. Cyzic.) ; ἐκ προγόνων παλλακίδων, of ritual prostitution, BCH 7.276 (Tralles).
ὁ, minion, Hsch., Phot.
Cret. for παραλαμβάνω.
κόρη, = Παλλάς, AP 6.247 (Phil.).
ὁ, the Palatine hill at Rome, Ael. VH 12.11, cf. DH. 1.31, Paus. 8.43.1.
ακος [prob. α], ὁ, youth, below the age of an ἔφηβος, Ael. Dion. Fr. 172 ; fem., girl, Gell. 4.3 ; — also πάλληξ, GDI 5704.7 (Samos, iii/ii BC), Ar.Byz. ap. Ammon. p. 37 V., Corn. ND 20, Hsch.

άδος, ἡ, Pallas, epith. of Athena, Παλλὰς Ἀθηναίη Il. 1.200, etc. ; later used alone, = Ἀθήνη, B. 5.92, Hdt. 5.77, IG1². 573, etc.
coin bearing the head of Pallas, Eub. 6 (pl.).
maiden-priestess, Str. 17.1.46, Eust. 1742.37. Pythag. name for five, Theol.Ar. 32. (Commonly deriv. from πάλλω, either as Brandisher of the spear, or παρὰ τὸ ἀναπεπάλθαι ἐκ τῆς κεφαλῆς τοῦ Διός, etc., Pl. Cra. 407a, EM 649.52, cf. Eust. 84.43, but prob. orig.
virgin, maiden, cf. πάλλας and v. παλλακή fin., πάλλαξ.)
αντος, ὁ, youth, Philistid. 1 J.
κρόμμυον (Ascalon), Hsch.
ῶνος, ὁ, name of month at Magnesia on the Maeander, Inscr.Magn. 2.3 (iv/iii BC).
ον, all-white, A. Eu. 352 (lyr.) ; δέρη, πούς, E. Med. 30, 1164 ; — written πάνλευκος, Orac. ap. Phleg. Fr. 37 J. (restd. for ζάλευκος from Zos. 2.6), Nonn. D. 7.218.
v. παλλάκιον.

ἡ, a peninsula and town of Chalcidice, Hdt. 7.123, Th. 1.56, etc. ; Maced. Βαλλήνη Eust. 1618.45 (whence the joke on Βαλλήναδε in Ar. Ach. 234, v. Sch. ad loc.). an Attic deme ; Παλληνεύς, ὁ, an inhabitant there of, Harp. ; fem. Παλληνὶς Ἀθηναίη, Hdt. 1.62, cf. IG1². 310.189 ; Παλλήναδε, to Pallene, v. supr. 1.
v. πάλλαξ.
name of a contest, Hsch. (Prob. Lat. Palilia.)
τό (for παλληκάριον, cf. παλλήκιον, πάλληξ), page, POxy. 1863.4.
πεμμάτιόν τι (Lacon.), Hsch.
(acc. sg., perh. for -ύριον), perh. name of a disease, BMus.Cat.Coins Ionia p. 70 (Ephesus) ; — also written παλυρριν, Num. Chron. 8 (1908).282 (ibid.).
ὄργανον βασανιστήριον, Hsch.

impf. ἔπαλλον E. Hec. 1158 ; Ep. πάλλον always in Hom. (v. infr.) ; aor.1 ἔπηλα S. El. 710 ; Ep. πῆλα Il. 6.474 ; Ep. aor.2 part. πεπαλών Hom. only in compd. ἀμπεπαλών ; — Med., aor.1 πήλασθαι Call. Jov. 64 ; πεπάλασθε, πεπαλάσθαι (v. παλάσσω) have been attributed to πάλλω· πεπάλεσθε, πεπαλέσθαι are conjectured as more prob. forms ; — Pass., pf. πέπαλμαι A. Ch. 410 (lyr.) ; aor.2 ἐπάλην (ἀν-) Str. 8.6.21 ; Ep. aor. πάλτο Il. 15.645 (in 13.643, 21.140, ἐπᾶλτο is from ἐφάλλομαι) : — poise, sway a missile before it is thrown, τὸ μὲν [ἔγχος] οὐ δύνατ’ ἄλλος Ἀχαιῶν πάλλειν, ἀλλά μιν οἶος ἐπίστατο πῆλαι Ἀχιλλεύς Il. 16.142 ; [αἰχμήν], ἣν… πάλλεν δεξιτερῇ 22.320 ; δοῦρε δύω… πάλλων 3.19 ; χερμάδιον… ὃ οὐ δύο γ’ ἄνδρε φέροιεν…, ὁ δέ μιν ῥέα πάλλε καὶ οἶος 5.304 ; ἄκοντα, λόγχην π., Pi. N. 3.45, E. IT 824 ; κεραυνόν Ar. Av. 1714. generally, sway, brandish, [σάκος] Hes. Sc. 321 ; ἰτύν, πέλτας, E. Ion 210 (lyr.), Ba. 783 ; toss a child, πῆλε χερσίν, of Hector and Astyanax, Il. 6.474, cf. E. Hec. 1158 ; Νὺξ ὄχημ’ ἔπαλλεν she drove it furiously, Id. Ion 1151. κλήρους ἐν κυνέῃ χαλκήρεϊ πάλλον shook the lots together in a helmet, Il. 3.316, cf. Od. 10.206 ; πάλλεν shook the lots, Il. 3.324, 7.181 ; but στάντες δ’ ὅθ’ αὐτοὺς οἱ… βραβῆς κλήροις ἔπηλαν καὶ κατέστησαν δίφρους ranged them by casting lots, S. El. 710 ; — Med., draw lots, ἔλαχον πολιὴν ἅλα παλλομένων I obtained the white sea when we cast lots, Il. 15.191 ; παλλόμενος κλήρῳ λάχον ἐνθάδ’ ἕπεσθαι 24.400, cf. Hdt. 3.128 ; — Pass., κλῆρος οὐκ ἐπάλλετο S. Ant. 396. Pass., swing, dash oneself, ἐν ἄντυγι πάλτο tripped on the shield-rim, Il. 15.645 ; quiver, leap, esp. in fear, ἐν δ’ ἐμοὶ αὐτῇ στήθεσι πάλλεται ἦτορ 22.452 ; πέπαλταί μοι φίλον κέαρ A. Ch. 410 ; of the person, παλλομένη κραδίην Il. 22.461 ; δείματι παλλόμεναι, οι, h.Cer. 293, Orac. ap. Hdt. 7.140, etc. ; γόνυ πάλλεται γερόντων Ar. Ra. 345 ; of dying fish, quiver, leap, Hdt. 1.141, cf. 9.120 ; καὶ πέραν πόντοιο πάλλοντ’ αἰετοί fly quivering even beyond the sea, Pi. N. 5.21 ; vibrate, of strings, Pl. Phd. 94c (ψάλλοιτο ap. Stob.) ; σκιρτητικὸν καὶ παλλόμενον τὸ νέον (etym. of Παλλάς) Corn. ND 20, cf. Pl. Cra. 407a.
intr., leap, bound, E. El. 435, Ar. Lys. 1304 (lyr.) ; quiver, quake, φρένα δείματι πάλλων S. OT 153 (lyr.) ; dash along, of horses, E. El. 477 (lyr.).
v. πανλώβητος.
ου, ὁ, (πάλλω) σεισμὸς π. an earthquake with violent shocks, Arist. Mu. 396a10.

γέρρον (i.e. Lat. parma), Hsch.
date, POxy. 519.18 (ii AD).
ή, όν, conveyed by palpitation, π. οἰώνισμα, title of a book, Suid. s.v. Ποσειδώνιος.

ὁ, quivering motion, πυγῆς Alciphr. 1.39 ; esp. pulsation, throbbing (on π. and σφυγμός cf. Gal. 8.716), φλεβῶν Hp. Acut. 37 ; ὑποχονδρίου Id. Epid. 1.26. β’ ; ὑπὸ κροτάφοισι Nic. Al. 27, cf. Th. 744 ; abs., palpitation of the heart, a disease, Arist. Resp. 479b21 ; twitching, Gal. 7.588. of natural phenomena, vibration, rapid motion, DS. 3.51, Nonn. D. 2.193, al. ; of meteors, Plu. Lys. 12 codd. ; impetus of a projectile, Ath.Mech. 37.8. in Epicur., internal vibration of bodies, Ep. I p. 8 U., cf. Id. ap. Placit. 1.12.5 (v.l. ἀποπαλμός).
ὁ, = Lat. parmularius, M.Ant 1.5.
υδος, ὁ, Lydian word, = βασιλεύς, Hippon. 1, 15 ; epith. of the king of the gods, Zeus, Lyc. 691 ; gen. πάλμυδος (Dind. for παλάμυδος) A. Fr. 437 ; acc. Πάλμυν pr. n. in Il. 13.792.
ες, throbbing, palpitating, of persons, Hp. Prorrh. 1.30 ; ἰδέαι DS. 3.50 ; π. νόσος Ph. 1.166 ; κινήσεις (opp. σφυγμώδεις) Gal. 8.722.
v. πηλός.

ὁ, (πάλλω I. 3) lot cast from a shaken helmet, A. Th. 458. Lyr., Ion., and Trag. generally, = κλῆρος, lot, τόνδε τὸν πάλον λαχόην Sappho 9, cf. A. Th. 376 ; πάλῳ λαχεῖν ib. 126, Hdt. 4.94, 153, Aen.Tact. 20.2 ; πάλῳ ἀρχὰς ἄρχειν Hdt. 3.80 ; πάλου κύρσαι A. Pers. 779 ; τύχης π. Id. Ag. 333 ; οὓς ἐκλήρωσεν π. E. Ion 416, cf. S. Ant. 275, dub. in E. IA 1151.
ballot, vote, A. Eu. 742, 753.

ὁ, = Lat. pālus, stake, PLond. 2.191.12 (ii AD), Aesop. 402, Edict.Diocl. 14.1, Zos. 2.35.
squad or team of gladiators, CIG 2663 (Halic.), Rev.Arch. 30 (1929).40 (Aphrodisias), etc.
τό, dial. form of βάλσαμον, Paus. 9.28.3.

εως, ἡ, rapid motion, vibration, ἀκτίνων Porph. ap. Eus. PE 3.11 ; in Epicur., = παλμός, internal vibration, Ep. 1 p. 12U.
brandishing, δοράτων EM 394.56 ; palpitation, τῆς καρδίας Chrysipp. Stoic. 2.247.
(< παλτόν) throw a dart, in aor.1 ἐπάλταξα, Hsch.
σεμίδαλις, Phot., Suid. ; cf. πολτάριον.
dub.sens., perh. scutch flax, BGU 1506.2.
v. πάλλω.

ή, όν, brandished, hurled, πῦρ S. Ant. 131 (lyr.). as Subst. παλτόν, τό, missile, dart, A. Fr. 16 ; of a light spear used by the Persian cavalry, X. Cyr. 4.3.9, 6.2.16, cf. Arr. Fr. 158 J. ; projectile discharged from a catapult, Id. Tact. 43.1.

strew, sprinkle, λεύκ’ ἄλφιτα πολλὰ πάλυνον (i.e. sprinkled in water, expld. by Sch. ἔμασσον, ἔφυρον) Il. 18.560 ; ἐπὶ δ’ ἄλφιτα λευκὰ παλύνειν Od. 10.520, cf. 11.28, etc. ; τι ἐπί τινι S. Ant. 247.
bestrew, besprinkle, with dat. of the thing sprinkled, παλύνας ἀλφίτου ἀκτῇ Od. 14.429 ; — Pass., ἁ σῦριγξ εὐρῶτι παλύνεται Theoc. 4.28. of liquids, κάρην ἱδρῶτι παλῦναι DP. 1049.
besmear, ἰξῷ AP 10.11 (Satyr.), cf. ARh. 3.1256 (Pass.).
cover lightly, χιὼν ἐπάλυνεν ἀρούρας Il. 10.7 ; νιφετῷ δ’ ἐπαλύνετο πάντα ARh. 3.69.
v. παλλυριν.

ατος, τό, (< *πάομαι) property, Schwyzer 657.39 (Tegea, iv BC), Theoc. Syrinx 12 (v.l. πῆμα) ; mostly pl., πατρῷα καὶ ματρῷα π. Schwyzer l.c. 6, cf. 27, Besant. Ara 5, AJPh 26.463 (Argos) ; of cattle, SIG 527.89 (Dreros, iii BC).
(< πᾶμα, φαγεῖν) confiscate, IG 9(1).334.41 (Locr., v BC, Pass.).
ίδος, ἡ, = βαμβάκιον, in pl., AP 6.254.6 (Myrin.).
ἡ, absolute monarchy, Arist. Pol. 1285b36, 1287a8.
ἡ, queen of all, all-powerful queen, Ar. Nu. 357, 1150, ARh. 4.382 ; of Persephone, IG 12(5).310.15 (Paros).
έως, ὁ, absolute monarch, Alc. 5, LXX Si. 50.15 (17) ; of Hadrian, Epigr.Gr. 990.3 (Balbilla).
ά, όν, utterly abominable, Ar. Lys. 969, Ec. 1043.
ου, ὁ, all-subduing, κεραυνός Pi. N. 9.24.
ές, wholly hurtful, Man. 4.31.
ὁ (sc. μήν), name of a month in Boeotia, IG 7.3321. Παμβοιώτια (sc. ἱερά), τά, festival of the United Boeotians, Plb. 4.3.5, 9.34.11, IG 7.3087 (Lebadea), Str. 9.2.29.
οἱ, United Boeotians, IG 7.2712.49 (Acraeph.).
ον, all-devouring, J. AJ 5.8.6, Ael. NA 1.27 (Sup.).
τό, all the herbage, τοῦ ἀγροῦ LXX Jb. 5.25.
ον, all-nourishing, ἄλσος A. Supp. 558 (lyr.), cf. Fr. 99.
ιδος, fem. of παμβώτωρ, Γᾶ S. Ph. 391 (lyr.).
ορος, ὁ, ἡ, = πάμβοτος, Cypr. 1.4 ; — fem. παμβῶτις, ιδος, Γᾶ S. Ph. 391 (lyr.).
αρος, ὁ, ἡ, all-blissful, Orph. H. 19.3, Hsch.
ον, = πάμμακαρ, JHS 22.97 (Pisidia), Hsch. s.v. πανόλβιος.
ον, all-vain, A. Ag. 388 codd. (leg. πᾶν μ.).
Adv. in which all fight, ADysc. Conj. 234.9.
ἡ, in pl., contests of all kinds, B. 12.76.
τό, = παγκράτιον, Phot., Suid.

ον, ready or sufficient for every battle, θράσος A. Ag. 169 (lyr.) ; epith. of Athena, Ar. Lys. 1321 ; esp. = παγκρατιαστής, fighting by all means, with all one΄s resources, Pl. Euthd. 271c, Theoc. 24.114, APl. 4.52 (Phil.), D.Chr. 8.19 ; τοὺς πέντε προεκαλεσάμην πάμμαχα Sammelb. 6222.22 (iii AD) ; so εἰς τὸ πάμμαχον ib. 26 ; ὁ παμμάχων κεραυνός AP 7.692 (Antip. or Phil.) ; metaph, οὐ φαῦλος ἀλλὰ π. ἀγὼν ὁ τῆς πολιτείας calling for all resources, Plu. 2.804b ; also π ; ἀτυχίη incompetence ready for anything, Hp. Praec. 13.
άλη, α, very great, immense, Pl. Phdr. 273a, Ti. 26e, etc. ; Sup. παμμέγιστος Ael. VH 10.2.
ες, = πάμμεγας, Pl. Prm. 164d, Lg. 913d, X. Mem. 3.6.13, Timocl. 8.14, D. 19.241, Arist. GA 745a34, al., Men. Her. 2 ; neut. as Adv., παμμέγεθες ἀναβοᾶν Aeschin. 2.106, cf. Men. Sam. 149.
ον, exceeding mild, Jo.Gaz. Ecphr. 1.75.
αινα, αν, all-black, ταῦροι Od. 3.6 ; ὄϊς 11.33 ; τράγος IG2². 1358 (iv BC) ; βόες Ael. NA 15.14.
Adv. of παμμελής II, Porph. Chr. 94.

ές, in all kinds of melodies, ὕμνοι LXX 3 Ma. 7.16.
II. with all the limbs, entire, ἱερεῖα Poll. 1.29.
ον, quite covered with, ὄρος π. τερμίνθων Thphr. HP 3.15.3.
(sc. βίβλος), ἡ, a book of verse in all kinds of metres, DL. 7.31.
ες, very long, prolonged, γόοι S. OC 1609 ; λόγος Pl. Plt. 286e ; ῥήσεις Id. Phdr. 268c ; ἐν χρόνοις π. Arist. Mete. 351b10 ; neut. as Adv., πάμμηκες διαφέρει ἔπαινος ἡδονῆς Max.Tyr. 7.7.
νύξ, ἡ, a night lighted by the full moon, Arat. 189.
ον, through all months, through the live-long year, S. El. 851 (lyr.).
σελήνη, = πανσέληνος, ἡ, Plu. 2.936a, Doroth. ap. Heph.Astr. 3.9 ; at full moon, ἱκετεῖαι cj. in Philod. Scarph. 114 (BCH 49.130).
ορος, ὁ, ἡ, all-inventive, μοῖρα βροτῶν Lyc. 490 ; Ἄρης Trag.Adesp. 129.9 (lyr.) ; Μοῖρα Orph. Fr. 47.
ἡ, = παμμήτωρ, h.Hom. 30.1, AP 5.164 (Mel.), v.l. in Orph. Fr. 168.27.
ιδος, ὁ, ἡ, all-knowing, all-planning, θεός Simon. 61.

ορος, ἡ, mother of all, γῆ A. Pr. 90, Ph. 1.32, cf. Orph. Fr. 168.27 ; θεᾷ παμμήτορι Ῥείῃ Epigr.Gr. 823.4.
a very mother, γυνὴ τοῦδε π. νεκροῦ S. Ant. 1282.
ον, all-abominable, Ar. Pax 183, Ra. 466, LXX 4 Ma. 10.17 (Sup.).
ές, mixed of all sorts, all-blended, βέλεα A. Pers. 269 (lyr.) ; στρατός Tim. Pers. 188 ; ἔθνη LXX 2 Ma. 12.13 ; σύμμαχοι DS. 29.19 ; βοή Lyc. 5.
ον, very small, Arist. PA 665b1, 669b29, Po. 1450b37, Gal. 18(2).753.
ον, = παμμιγής, ὄχλος A. Pers. 53 (anap.) ; ἐπίκουροι ib. 903 (lyr.), cf. Aq. Ps. 77 (78).45, Vett.Val. 15.15.
ον, all-hapless, S. OC 161 (lyr.).
ον, assuming all forms, of Proteus, Theol.Ar. 7 ; ἰδέαι Dam. Pr. 311.
ον, all-musical, ἁρμονία, χορεία, Ph. 1.625, 526 ; ἀνήρ Calder Philadelphia and Montanism 35.
ον, all-countless, Ph. 1.329.
ά, όν, = παμμίαρος, Ar. Lys. 969.
ον, all-remembering, πραπίδες Maiist. 46.
ές, wholly passive, Plot. 1.8.3 ; ὕλη Iamb. Myst. 3.29. sens. obsc., = παθικός, Man. 4.311. name of a plaster, Aët. 15.15.
Adv. with all their children, DC. 41.9 ; cf. παγγυναικί.
ον, very old, Pl. Tht. 181b, Arist. Metaph. 1074b1, cj. in ib. 983b28 ; opp. καινός, Plu. Cat. Ma. 1.
Adv. altogether to the contrary, CratesCom. 15.
ον, gen. ονος, possessing all, Hsch. (cj. for Πάμπανον).

Adv., (< πᾶς) wholly, altogether, with Verb, Il. 1.422, Od. 2.49, Hes. Op. 275, 302, Sappho 51.4, Pi. O. 2.69, Emp. 140 ; with Adj., π. ὀϊζυρός Od. 20.140, cf. E. Med. 1091 (anap.) ; οὐ π. ἀληθέες Call. Jov. 60 ; with Adv., π. ἐτήτυμον Il. 13.111 ; preceded by a neg., οὐδέ τι πάμπαν not at all, by no means, 9.435, cf. 21.338 ; with the Art., τὸ π. E. Rh. 855, Fr. 196 ; rare in early Prose, Hdt. 2.45, X. Ages. 11.4, Aen.Tact. 16.2 ; τὸ π. Pl. Plt. 270e, Ti. 41b ; freq. in Arist., as Cael. 286a6, al. as Adj., πάμπαν τὸ λοιπόν IG1². 6.117.
Adv. strengthd. for πάνυ, dub. in DC. 56.30.
ές, all-persuasive, Pi. P. 4.184.
Adv., = πάμπαν, entirely, Thgn. 615, A. Pers. 729 (troch.), Fr. 156, S. Aj. 916 ; — also παμπηδόν, παμπηδονίς, Theognost. Can. 163.
= παμπήδην.
= παμπήδην.
ἡ, (< πέπαμαι) entire possession, full property, A. Th. 817, E. Ion 1305, Ar. Ec. 868.
η, ον, in large quantity, number, χρήματα Hdn. 5.6.5 ; ἄργυρος Ael. NA 10.50 ; πάμπλειστα δαπανήσας DC. 76.16.
ονος, ὁ, ἡ, much greater, ὄγκος τῆς φωνῆς Arist. Aud. 804a15.
Adv. strengthd. for ἐμπλήγδην, Suid.
Adv. with the whole multitude, Ev. Luc. 23.18, DC. 75.9.

ές, in or with their whole multitude, παμπληθεῖς Ἀρκάδες X. HG 6.5.26. = πάμπολυς, very numerous, multitudinous, μεταβολαί Pl. Lg. 782b, cf. Tht. 156b ; γεωργίαι D. 19.145 ; πονηρίαι Id. 21.19 ; χρήματα prob. in DS. 14.13 ; κραυγαί POxy. 1242.54 (i AD) ; c. gen., παμπληθεῖς Ἀργείων Isoc. 12.169 ; with sg., π. ἂν τὸ γένος ἦν (sc. τῶν ἰχθύων) Arist. HA 567b2 ; π. κεκτήμεθα τὴν οὐσίαν a vast amount of…, Isoc. 15.154 ; πῦρ π. Arist. Mir. 833a20. neut. as Adv., entirely, παμπληθὲς ἀπέσχεν D. 19.19, cf. DC. 55.20.
ἡ, multitude, οἰκετῶν S. Fr. 373.4.
= παμπληθής II, παμπληθὺν θρήνων γόον Epigr. in Abh.Berl.Akad. 1909 (2).62.
to be plentiful, Aq. Jb. 36.31.
ον ; ἄεθλα π. contests in which blows fall thick, S. Tr. 505 (lyr.).
ες, quite full, Arist. GC 325a29 (v.l. -πληθές).
ον, very rich, Pl. Lg. 743c, DC. 40.12.
ον, = παμπλούσιος, ὄλβος S. Fr. 646.5 ; π. ἐν πλούτῳ γενέσθαι Gal. Anim. Pass. 9.

ον, all-variegated, of rich and varied work, πέπλοι Od. 15.105, cf. Il. 6.289 ; of sacred vases, Pi. N. 10.36 ; νεβρῶν π. στολίδες E. Hel. 1359 (lyr.) ; of persons, π. περὶ πᾶσαν τέχνην καὶ πρᾶξιν Vett.Val. 17.16. metaph, ὕφασμα, of the universe, Ph. 1.651, cf. 654 ; manifold, ἀλλοιότητας παμποικίλους (παμποικίλας codd.) Pl. Ti. 82b.
εως, ὁ, ἡ, prevailing in all cities, universal, νόμος dub. in S. Ant. 614 (lyr., πάμπολύ γ’ Heath).

πόλλη (v. infr.), πολυ, very great, large, or numerous, κατάγελως Ar. Eq. 320 ; γῆς πλῆθος Pl. Lg. 677e ; στράτευμα X. An. 2.4.26 ; τύχη Pl. Lg. 640d (but πάμπολλος as fem., Luc. Cyn. 1, Ael. VH 4.8, ADysc. Pron. 89.12, Synt. 36.27) ; in pl., very many, Ar. Pax 694, Pl. R. 373c, etc. neut. πάμπολυ, as Adv., very much, Id. Sph. 255d, etc. ; cf. πάμπολις.

ον, thoroughly depraved, Ar. Ach. 854, Nu. 1319, Pl. R. 489d, D. 18.119, Phld. Rh. 1.344S. of things, very bad, ὄψον Epich. 87 ; διάθεσις Phld. Ir. p. 77 W. Adv. -ρως, ἔχειν to be very ill, Luc. Abd. 14, cf. Jul. Or. 8.241b.
ές, all-destroying, prob. for παμπρόσθη in A. Ag. 714 (lyr.).
ον, all-purple, Pi. O. 6.55.
ἡ, all-venerable, AP 6.281 (Leon.).
ἡ, unreserved sale of property, Poll. 7.196, al.
ον, all-conspicuous, ἕδραι A. Ag. 117 (lyr.).
v. παμπορθής.
ον, all face, χρῆμα Plot. 6.7.15.
εως, ὁ, lord of all, Ph. 1.642.
η, ον, the very first, first of all, Il. 7.324, 9.93 ; neut. πάμπρωτον as Adv., Od. 4.577 ; ἐπεὶ π. εἶδον φέγγος Pi. P. 4.111 ; also in pl. -πρωτα, Il. 4.97, 17.568 ; Sup. παμπρώτιστα ARh. 4.1693.
ον, full of pus, πτύσιες Hp. Coac. 373.
ον, very miserable, Arch.Pap. 1.428 (iv AD).

ον, all-devouring, voracious, ὁ π. Ἀλκμάν Alcm. 33.4 ; πῦρ E. Med. 1187.
omnivorous, ζῷα (opp. ζῳοφάγα, καρποφάγα) Arist. Pol. 1256a25, cf. HA 488a15, 593b25 ; τῶν π., οἷς πάντα ἐσθίειν νόμος Jul. Or. 6.192d ; Comp., τὰ παμφαγώτερα ποικιλώτερα Arist. GA 786a34 ; Sup., παμφαγώτατον πάντων ὁ βοῦς Thphr. HP 9.15.4.
ές, all-shining, radiant, of fire, S. Ph. 728 (lyr.) E. Tr. 548 (lyr.) ; of the sun, Id. Med. 1251 (lyr.), cf. Ar. Av. 1709, IG 12(5).891.3 (Tenos), etc. ; of honey, bright, pure, A. Pers. 612.

only pres. and impf. (παμφαίνεσκε Eratosth. 17), shine or beam brightly, of burnished metal (cf. παμφανόων), ἧλοι χρύσειοι πάμφαινον Il. 11.30 ; σάκος χαλκῷ παμφαῖνον 14.11 ; τεύχεσι παμφαίνων, of Achilles, 19.398 ; of a star, ὅς τε μάλιστα λαμπρὸν παμφαίνησι or -ῃσι (Ep. for παμφαίνει or -ῃ) 5.6 ; πρῶτον παμφαίνων Hes. Op. 567 ; στήθεσι παμφαίνοντες with their breasts white-gleaming, i.e. naked, Il. 11.100 ; ὕπερθε κέρα πάμφαινεν ἰδέσθαι Epic. in Arch.Pap. 7.3 ; cited as a recondite word by Phld. Po. 2.40. (Redupl. form of φαίνω.)

redupl. form like παιφάσσω (cf. παπταλάω, παπταίνω), gaze in astonishment, Ion. word, Hippon. 131, Anacr. 160, Herod. 4.77 ; πάντοσε παμφαλόωντες Eryc. ap. Sch. ARh. 2.127 ; aor.1 ἐπαμφάλησα· ἐθαύμασα, Hsch. ; — Med., ἄγχι παμφαλώμενος Lyc. 1433.
τὴν πομφόλυγα, Sophr. 152.
= τρέμω, Hsch.
Egypt., = ἀείζων τὸ μέγα, Ps.-Dsc. 4.88.

gen. ωντος, fem. παμφανόωσα, Ep. part. as if from παμφανάω (cf. παμφανάᾳ· λάμπει, Hsch.), bright-shining, radiant, of burnished metal, αἴγλη [χαλκοῦ] Il. 2.458 ; τεύχεα 5.295, 18.144 ; ἠέλιος Od. 13.29 ; αἰθήρ Emp. 98.2.
ον, skilled in all charms or drugs, of Medea, Pi. P. 4.233.
ές, = παμφαής, S. El. 105 (lyr.).
ές, all-bearing, all-including, Gal. 19.469.
ον, all-speaking, Zonar.
ον, all-destroying, μόρος A. Ch. 296.
εως, ἡ, destroyer of all, στάσις B. Fr. 20.2.
ον, with or of all sounds, Hsch.
Adv., = παντάπασι, Hsch.
ον, beloved of all, ὄλβος prob. in A. Eu. 536 (lyr.) ; Sup. -έστατος PGrenf. 2.92.11 (vi AD).
ον, all-blazing, βωμοί S. Ant. 1006 ; π. πῦρ Id. El. 1139, Axionic. 4.11.
α, ον, very dreadful, Tab. Defix. Aud. 38.11 (Alexandria, iii AD), Gloss.
η, ον, all-feeding, παλάμη AP 7.698 (Christod.), cf. Epigr.Gr. 1036 (Nicomedia, dub.), Eust. 978.4.

ον, all-bearing, all-productive, χώρη παμφορωτέρη Hdt. 7.8. αʹ, cf. Hp. Coac. 502, Pl. Lg. 704c, Thphr. HP 3.2.6 ; γαῖα A. Pers. 618 ; ἔτος Orph. Fr. 251 ; παμφορώτατον κτῆμα ὃ καλεῖται φίλος X. Mem. 2.4.7.
bearing all things with it, π. χέραδος a mixed mass of rubbish, Pi. P. 6.13 ; metaph, π. θεωρήματα Pall. in Hp. 2.114 D.
ον, wise in all things, Tz. H. 6.595 (Sup.).
Adv. in total rout, Oppian. H. 2.548 (v.l. παμφύρδην).
ές, combining all natures, δέμας, of Pan, IG4²(1).130.19 (Epid.).
ἡ, Pamphylia, Th. 1.100, Pl. R. 615c, etc.
ου, ὁ, President of the Provincial Council of Pamphylia, BCH 23.302 (Termessus), IGRom. 3.474 (Balbura).

ον, (< φυλή, φῦλον) of mingled tribes or races, γένος Pl. Plt. 291a ; πόλις Poll. 9.21 ; π. θῆρες Ar. Av. 1063. Πάμφυλοι, οἱ, one of the three Dorian tribes, Hdt. 5.68, IG4²(1).71.49 (Epid.), SIG 1025.8 (Cos), etc. ; gen. pl. Παμφυλᾶν IG 4.598 (Argos) ; Παμφύλεων SIG 1027.4 (Cos.). Pamphylian, Hdt. 1.28, al., Pl. R. 614b, etc.
ον, mixed of all sorts, γέννημα Ph. 1.148, cf. 2.53, Longin. 9.7, Oppian. H. 1.779 ; neut. pl. as Adv., confusedly, S. Ichn. 232.

ον, with all tones, full-toned or many-toned, ἔντεα αὐλῶν Pi. O. 7.12 ; μέλος Id. P. 12.19 ; αὐλῶν ὁμοκλαί Id. I. 5 (4).27 ; ὑμέναιοι Id. P. 3.17 ; generally, expressive, χεῖρες APl. 4.290 (Antip.) ; π. οἶνος noisy, Philox. 16.
ον, much-blamed, Man. 4.316.
ορος, ὁ, one that blames all, Man. 4.58.
Adv. with all the votes, π. νικᾶν AP 11.239 (Lucill.), cf. Sch. Ar. Eq. 525, etc. ; Dor. παμψαφεί Polus ap. Stob. 3.9.51.
ον, = παμψέκτωρ, Ptol. Tetr. 160.
ον, (< ψυχή) in full life, π. ἀνάσσει, of Amphiaraus, S. El. 841 (lyr., also expld. by Sch. as ΄ruling over all the shades’ or ΄immortal΄, = πασῶν ψυχῶν ἀνάσσει, cf. Od. 11.483sq., A. Ch. 355).
own, possess, Tab.Heracl. 1.168 ; — also παμωχιῶν· κεκτημένος, Hsch.
ὁ, Dor. for Παμοῦχος, owner, Hsch.

gen. Πανός, dat. Πανί (uncontr. Πάονι IG 5(2).556 (Melpea, vi BC)), ὁ, Pan, Πᾶνα δέ μιν καλέεσκον, ὅτι φρένα πᾶσιν ἔτερψεν h.Hom. 19.47, cf. 5, Hdt. 2.145, 6.105, etc. ; ὦ Πὰν Ἀρκαδίας μεδέων Pi. Fr. 95, cf. Theoc. 1.123, etc. ; Π. κεροβάτας Ar. Ra. 230 (lyr.) ; pl. Πᾶνες Id. Ec. 1069, Theoc. 4.63, DS. 1.88 ; dat. pl. Πᾶσιν Id. 5.28 ; Πανὸς γόνος, σπέρμα, in magic, PMagPar. 1.2306, 2996 ; Πανὸς κέρατα, = γλυκυσίδη, Ps.-Dsc. 3.140.
ον, quite or very soft, Luc. Rh. Pr. 11.
ἡ, perfect goodness, Theag. ap. Stob. 3.1.117.
ον, also η, ον, absolutely good, Cratin. 434, Pl. Ep. 354e, Simp. in Epict. p. 76 D.

ές, all-hallowed, Call. Fr. 1.36P. ; κόρη (Cassandra) D.Chr. 11.153 ; ἱέρειαι Poll. 1.35, Hsch. (παναιεῖς cod.) ; ἱερωσύνη Jul. Or. 5.160b (Sup.) ; ἱερεύς IG 3.716 ; = Lat. sacrosanctus, of the Rom.
Tribuni Plebis, DH. 6.89, 8.87, Plu. Cam. 20.
under an ἄγος, Philonid. 5, Man. 4.120.
ον, most reverend, Man. 2.433.
v. παναγιστία.
α, ον, all-holy, LXX 4 Ma. 7.4.
ἡ, = παναγία, dub.sens., Hsch.
= παναγής 1, ὄμμα Callistr. Stat. 10 ; κήρυκες Sch. Aeschin. 1.20.
ἡ, = πανήγυρις, Schwyzer 657.21 (Tegea, iv BC, pl.).
ὁ, = πανηγύριος, name of month at Tegea, IG 5(2).3.30 (iv BC).
εως, ἡ, = παναγορία, IG 5(2).3.26 (Tegea, iv BC).
ον, taking all kinds of game, νευρά AP 6.75 (Paul. Sil.).
έως, ὁ, one who catches everything, παναγρέος έλπίδα Μοίρης AP 7.609 (Paul. Sil.) ; φυλάκων… παναγρέα κανθόν ib. 5.218 (Id.).
ον, quite wild or savage, Opp. C. 2.45, dub. in Ps.-Phoc. 202.
ίος, ἡ, = λεβητάριον, IG 4.1588.18 (Aegina), Poll. 10.165 (v.l. ταν-).

τό, fishing- or huntingnet, Opp. C. 1.150, H. 3.83.
large hen-coop in which fowls are fattened, Ath. 1.22d.
ον, (< ἄγρα) catching all, λίνον π., of a large fishing-net, Il. 5.487 ; δίκτυον Ath. 1.25b ; metaph, λίνῳ θανάτοιο π. Tryph. 674.
ον, all-wakeful, μέριμνα AP 7.195 (Mel.).
v. πανηγυριάρχας.
v. πανηγύριος.
v. πανήγυρις.
passing through all trials, epith. of martyrs, PMasp. 162.8 (vi AD).
ές, cruel, μοῖραι Epigr.Gr. 403.1 ; μόχθος Antioch.Astr. in Cat.Cod.Astr. 1.112.
ές, all-undigested, δόρπος Nic. Al. 66.
ον, unarmed, ὤμοσαν ἀγελάοι π. SIG 527.11 (Crete, iii BC).
ον, utterly lawless, cj. for πανάθεσμος in Man. 4.56.
ον, = παναθέσμιος, Opp. C. 2.438, 3.224.
ον, (< θέσσασθαι) quite inexorable, Hsch. (παναίθετος cod.).

(sc. ἱερά), τά, Panathenaea, festival at Athens, Hdt. 5.56 ; τὰ μεγάλα Π. Th. 5.47, Lys. 21.1, Isoc. 12.17, IG1². 10.2, 304.6 ; τὰ μικρὰ Π. Lys. 21.2 (also τὰ κατ’ ἐνιαυτόν IG2². 334.32), cf. Ar. Nu. 988, And. 1.28, etc. ; also at Ilium, festival of Athena Ilias, SIG 355.18 (iv/iii BC).
ή, όν, of, for, or at the Panathenaea, ἡ π. πομπή Th. 1.20, etc. ; ὁ Π. (sc. λόγος), name of a speech of Isocrates ; τὰ π. name of vases given as prizes at the P., Posidon. 25 J.
ὁ (sc. μήν), month at Ilium, Supp.Epigr. 4.663.
ΐδος, ἡ, four-year period between celebrations of the Great Panathenaea, IG 3.1202. as Adj., Παναθηναῒς σκάφη ship borne in procession at the Panathenaea, SIG 894 (iii AD).
οἱ, celebrators of Παναθήναια, at Teos, CIG 3073 ; at Rhodes, IG 12(1).107, al.
α, ον, all-wretched, A. Ch. 695, S. OC 1110, E. Hec. 658, Timocl. 25 ; in late Prose, Ph. 1.542.
εσσα, εν, all-shining, κῆπος AP 9.806.
= παγκακοῦργος, Hsch.
η, ον, all-revered, Epigr.Gr. 228b (Ephesus).
η, ον, all-blazing, κόρυθες Il. 14.372.

ον, shot with many colours, glancing, ζωστήρ Il. 4.186, 215, 10.77 ; θώρηξ 11.374 ; σάκος 13.552, Hes. Sc. 139 ; star-spangled, π. οὐρανός Orph. H. 4.7, Fr. 238. metaph, manifold, βάγματα A. Pers. 636 (lyr.).
ἡ, full vigour of the senses, DL. 10.65 (Meibom for ἀναισθ-).
ον, all-impious, Hsch. (-αίγ- cod.).
ες, utterly ugly, τὴν ἰδέαν Arist. EN 1099b4, cf. Poll. 6.163.
ἡ, absolute ugliness, Tz. H. 3.216.
ον, = παναίσχης, D.Chr. 31.35, Ptol. Tetr. 172 ; Sup., παναισχίστη τέρψις AP 6.163 (Mel.). Adv. -ρως Plb. 4.58.11, Tz. H. 6.44.

ον, (< αἰτία) cause of all, Ζεύς A. Ag. 1486 ; ἓν π. Dam. Pr. 37.
to whom all the guilt belongs, opp. μεταίτιος, A. Eu. 200.
τά, meeting and festival of the Aetolian League, SIG 563 (Teos, iii BC), IG 9(1).411 ; — also Παναιτώλια, τά, Poll. 6.163 ; — also in sg., Liv. 31.29.
ές, all-barren, Nic. Th. 612.

ἡ, universal remedy, panacea, Longin. 38.5, Ph. 1.215, Gal. 13.766. name of a healing herb or its juice (cf. πανακής II), Call. Ap. 40, etc. ; πανακείας ῥίζα Gal. 14.156 ; Hercules’ woundwort, Opopanax hispidus, Thphr. HP 9.15.7. = λιγυστικόν, Laserpitium garganicum, Ps.-Dsc. 3.51. = ἄρκιον, Id. 4.106. Pythag. name for six, Theol.Ar. 38. personified as daughter of Asclepius, Hp. Jusj., Ar. Pl. 702, 730.
τό, = πανάκεια I. 2, Nic. Th. 508.
τό, v. πανακής II.
ές, free from all care, σαύρη, of the salamander, prob. in Nic. Al. 538.
ἡ, = πανάκεια I. 2, APl. 4.273 (Crin.).
ον, all-uncontaminated, θεός Corp.Herm. 18.12 ; Ἄπολλον PMagBerol. 2.87.

ές, (< ἄκος) all-healing, π. πάντων φάρμακον ἁσοφία Call. Epigr. 47.4, cf. Ph. 1.455 (Sup.) ; ποτάμιον π. πρὸς τὰς τῶν θρεμμάτων νόσους Str. 6.3.9 ; λύπης πανακές Epicur. Fr. 154. πάνακες, ους, τό, all-heal, Ferulago galbanifera, Hp. Mul. 2.201, Thphr. HP 9.7.2, etc. ; π. Ἀσκληπίειον Aesculapius’ all-heal, Echinophora tenuifolia, ib. 9.8.7, 9.11.1 ; π. Ἡράκλειον, = πανάκεια I. 2a, ib. 9.11.3, Dsc. 3.48 ; π. Κενταύρειον Centaury, Centaurea salonitana, Plin. HN 25.33, Sch. Nic. Th. 564 ; π. λεπτόφυλλον feverfew, Erythraea Centaurium, Thphr. HP 9.11.4 ; π. Χειρώνειον elecampane, Inula Helenium, ib. 9.11.1 ; also, = Chiron΄s all-heal, Hypericum olympicum, Nic. Th. 565 (cf. 500), Dsc. 3.50, Gal. 12.95.
(sc. οἶνος), ὁ, wine prepared with πάνακες, Dsc. 5.62.
ον, in Nic. Th. 626, π. κονίλη, expld. by Sch. either as ἡ ἐπὶ πάσῃ ἀκτῇ φυομένη or as a poet. form of πανάκειος ; cf. πάνακτος· ὀρίγανος, Hsch.
ορος, ὁ, strengthd. for ἀλάστωρ, AP 9.269 (Antip. Thess.).
ές, all true, π. κακόμαντις Ἐρινύς A. Th. 722 (lyr.). Adv. -θῶς Id. Supp. 86 (lyr.). of things, absolutely true or real, ἡδονή Pl. R. 583b, cf. Iamb. Protr. 4 (Sup.).
ον, gen. ονος, roving all about, ψυχή Procl. H. 3.15.
ές, all-healing, Nic. Th. 939.
ές, all-powerful, v.l. for παναρκής, A. Th. 166 (lyr.) ; Sup., of a poultice, Aët. 3.177 (sed cf. παναρκής).
ές, all-purple-dyed, Xenoph. 3.3.
ον, all-catching, ἄτη A. Ag. 361 (anap.).

title of Zeus in Caria, BCH 12.254, al., Supp.Epigr. 4.263.3, al. (Panamara) ; — also Πανήμερος, ib. 288, al. ; Πανημέριος, ib. 304, al. (ibid.) ; hence Παναμάρεια, τά, his festival, BCH 11.376. Supp.Epigr. 4.301.12 (ibid.).
ον, all-unsmiling, πρόσωπα Opp. C. 3.141.
ον, all-implacable, δράκαινα Opp. C. 3.223.
ον, allunmerciful, ἦτορ Opp. C. 2.203.
Dor. for πανημέριος.
ον, Dor. for πανήμερος.
τά, festival at Thespiae, Schwyzer 491.11 (v. Πάναμος).
ον, without any share in, ἠελίοιο AP 14.125 (Metrod.).

ὁ, name of a month, at Argos, Mnemos. 44.51 ; at Epidaurus, IG (1).117.9, al. ; at Megara, ib. 7.188 ; at Thespiae, ib. 1720 ; — also written Πάνεμος (Boeot.), Plu. Cam. 19 ; Πάνημος, D. 18.157 (Corinth.), Call. Epigr. 46, IG 11(2).203 A 31 (Delos, iii BC), PCair. Zen. 20.5 (iii BC) ; — hence Πανάμια, τά, festival at Thespiae, Schwyzer 491.11.
ον, all-blameless, Simon. 5.17.
παντοδύναμον, Phot. ; πάντα δυνατόν, Suid.
ακος, ὁ, = πάνακες or πανάκεια, Dsc. 2.163, 3.51, Ps.-Dsc. 3.48, Philagr. ap. Orib. 5.19.12, etc.
ον, all-worthy, Opp. C. 3.408.
ον, sung by all, APl. 4.71, Dioscorus in PLit. Lond. 100 C 6.
ον, all-tender or delicate, ἀνδρὶ δέμας εἰκυῖα νέῳ…, παναπάλῳ Od. 13.223 [παν-, metri gr.] ; γυναῖκες Ph. 2.432.
ον, without tasting, ἐδωδῆς Nic. Al. 592.
ές, f.l. for παναπευθής, Parm. 4.6.
ον, all-unbounded, Opp. C. 2.517.
ον, gen. ονος, = παναπείριτος, ὦ π. Κρονίων Pi. Pae. 8.24.
ές, f.l. for ταλαπενθής, APl. 4.265.
ές, utterly inscrutable, ἀταρπός Parm. 4.6.
ον, gen. ονος, all-harmless, Hes. Op. 811 ; of Apollo, AP 9.525.17.
ές, all-unmutilated, κεφαλαί Call. Cer. 126.
ον, all-untrustworthy, Phld. Rh. 1.232 S. (Sup.).
ον, all-astounded, Socr. Ep. 36.
ον, = πανήπορος (on which Hsch. gives it as a gloss), Ascl. in Metaph. 421.29.
ον, entirely opposite, οἶμος (of heavenly bodies) Man. 6.295.
ον, all-hapless, ὤ μοι ἐγὼ πανάποτμος Il. 24.255, cf. 493.
ον, all-unheard of, Phot., Suid., restd. in Philic. in Stud.Ital. 9.48.
ον, all-silver, κρητήρ Od. 9.203, 24.275, Antim. 15, cf. S. Fr. 378.3.
ονος, all-heroic, in pl., Dioscorus in PLit. Lond. 99.9.

ον, model of all virtue, Phld. Rh. 2.203S., Ph. 1.451, Luc. Philops. 6, S.E. M. 9.152, IG 14.2098, CIG 4413 (Iotape) ; also ἡ π. σου φιλία PSI 1.98.3 (vi AD). Adv. -τως CIG 4150 (Amastris). πανάρετος, ἡ, a Book of Fortunes, Paul.Al. K. 2.
ἡ, wholly enviable, Ἀριάδνη Dioscorus in PLit. Lond. 99.4.
τό, = Lat. panarium (Gr. ἀρτοφόριον), S.E. M. 1.234.
ον (fem. -αρίστη IG 12(7).296 (Amorgos)), best of all, Hes. Op. 293, Phld. Rh. 2.198 S., AP 11.394, Luc. Fug. 30.
ἡ, self-sufficiency, etym. of πανάκεια I. 3, Theol.Ar. 38.
νόσου, utter, complete, dub. in A. Ch. 70 (lyr.).
ές, = πανταρκής, θεοί A. Th. 166 (lyr.) ; Ἠέλιος the sun that shines on all alike, Call. Fr. 48.1, cf. Suid. s.v. ; Sup., of a poultice, Lycus ap. Orib. 9.26.1 ; cf. παναλκής.

ον, embracing all modes or scales, in neut. of a style of Music, οὐκ ἄρα πολυχορδίας γε οὐδὲ παναρμονίου ἡμῖν δεήσει ἐν ταῖς ᾠδαῖς τε καὶ μέλεσι Pl. R. 399c, cf. 404d ; [ὄργανα] π. ib. 399d ; αὐτὰ τὰ π. ibid. ; τὸ π. τὸ καινόν Alex. 298 ; π. ὄργανον DC. 74.3. metaph, complex, elaborate, ποικίλῃ μὲν ποικίλους ψυχῇ καὶ π. διδοὺς λόγους opp. ἁπλοῦς, Pl. Phdr. 277c, cf. Iamb. Myst. 5.21 ; π. τι χρῆμα ἡ ὄρχησις Luc. Salt. 72 ; ψυχαὶ π. διὸ παντοδαπῶς ἔστιν ἀκούειν ἀμφοτέρων, of Homer and Plato, Olymp. Vit. Pl. p. 4 W.
harmonious, χορός Ph. 2.399 ; ἀστέρων στρατιά ib. 242 ; συζυγία τῶν τεττάρων δυνάμεων ib. 136 ; ἑβδομάς, ὀγδοάς, ib. 166, Pythag. ap. Theol.Ar. 54 ; τετράχορδον, of Diocletian and his associates, Jul. Caes. 315c ; π. ἐρωαί, of the song of the Muses, Orac. ap. Porph. Plot. 22 ; neut. as Adv., π. ᾄδειν Philostr. Im. 2.1.
ή, όν, extremely ancient, πίναξ Chron.Lind. B. 88.
ον, = παναρχαϊκός, γράμματα Poll. 5.150.
ον, all-powerful, ruling all, θρόνοι S. OC 1293.
οντος, ὁ, ruler of all, Ph. 2.452 (pl.).
ές, all-unharmed, Hsch.
Adv. very readily, only in Sup. -έστατα Tz. H. 9.10.
ὁ, giving security, epith. of Zeus and Poseidon at Mytilene, Ath.Mitt. 24.358 (Mytil.).
v. πηνῖτις.
ές, all-exact, infallible, φάτις Keil-Premerstein Erster Bericht p. 9 (Troketta) ; μνῆμα AP 7.594 (Jul.) ; neut. as Adv., ARh. 4.1382.
ἡ, fount of light, Ph. 1.7.
ές, allbright, radiant, Orph. H. 10.3.
ον, all-sleepless, Oppian. H. 2.659.
ές, all-invisible, Eratosth. Cat. 23.
ικος, ὁ, ἡ, completely severed from companions of his own age, ἦμαρ ὀρφανικὸν παναφήλικα παῖδα τίθησιν Il. 22.490.
ον, allimperishable, ἦμαρ AP 7.14 (Antip.Sid.).
ον, allbountiful, epith. of Isis, POxy. 1380.88 (ii AD).
ον, all-inevitable, βρόχος AP 9.396 (Paul. Sil.) ; ζεῦγμα IG 3.1339.
ον, all-leafless, h.Cer. 452.

οἱ, all the Achaeans, Il. 2.404, al. ; fem. Παναχαιά, ἡ, epith. of Demeter, Paus. 7.24.3 ; of Artemis, BCH 25.350 (Delph.) ; — also Παναχαιὶς γῆ, all Achaea, ARh. 1.243 ; Παναχαιΐς, epith. of Athena, Paus. 7.20.2.
ον, doomed to an untimely end, ἀλλ’ ἕνα παῖδα τέκεν π. Il. 24.540 ; π. ῥυτίς AP 5.263.5 (Paul. Sil.).
ον, = παναώριος, Epigr.Gr. 313.3 (Smyrna).
ές, all-knowing, Δημόκριτος Tz. H. 4.529.
ον, richly carved, Pi. Fr. 75.5.

Ion. -ίη, ἡ, (< δαίς) complete banquet at which no one and nothing fails, Hdt. 5.20, Ar. Pax 565, Is. Fr. 100, Plu. 2.1102a, Supp.Epigr. 4.304.6 (Panamara), Alciphr. 3.18 ; — also πανδαίσιον, τό, Phot., Suid.
ου, ὁ, biting all, of Cato, Epigr. ap. Plu. Cat. Ma. 1.

ον, all-tearful, ὀδύρματα S. Tr. 50.
all-bewept, most miserable, γένος A. Th. 654 ; βιοτά S. Ph. 689 (lyr.) ; ἐφαμέρων ἔθνη E. Or. 976 (lyr.).
[prob. δᾰ], ον, (< δηλέομαι, δάλλει) = ἐπίτριπτος, Hippon. 2 (vv. ll. πανδάληκτος, πανδαύληκτος, whence Bgk. proposes πανδαύχνητος, = πανδάφνωτος, all laurel-crowned).

ορος, ὁ, (< δαμάω) the all-subduer, all-tamer, of sleep, Il. 24.5, Od. 9.373 ; of time, Simon. 4.5, B. 12.205, Epigr.Gr. 1050 (Ephesus) ; π. δαίμων S. Ph. 1467 (anap.) ; κεραυνός Luc. Tim. 2, etc. ; — pecul. fem. πανδαμάτειρα, Orph. H. 10.26, Epigr.Gr. 434.6 (Petra), IG 12(5).303 (Paros) ; πανδαμάτωρ μοῖρα Arist. Pepl. 43.
πανδαμί, πάνδαμος, v. πανδημεί, πανδημί, πάνδημος.
ον, all-cowardly, all-miserable, Emp. 141, Opp. C. 3.230.
ον, all-dreaded, Lyr.Adesp. 140, dub. in Pi. Fr. 189.

ον, all-dreadful, terrible, πάνδεινον ἡ ἀδικία Pl. R. 610d, cf. 605c ; πρᾶγμα D. 54.33, cf. Men. Sam. 212, Ruf. Fr. 69 ; πάνδεινα πεπονθέναι Luc. Prom. 8 ; πάνδεινόν [ἐστι] it is outrageous, D. 23.79, cf. PTeb. 27.34 (ii BC), Phld. Ir. p. 86 W.
very able, c. inf., Pl. Plt. 290b ; ironically, D. 19.120.
ἡ, pecul. fem. of πανδέκτης, κοιλίη π. Hp. Ep. 23.

ου, ὁ, all-receiver ; in pl. πανδέκται, οἱ, name of a Universal Dictionary or Encyclopedia, such as those compiled by Tiro and Dorotheus, Gell. 13.9. in pl., also, the Pandects, i.e. the law-books of Justinian, Cod.Just. 1.17.1.12, al. ; sg., ὁ π., = Digesta, Id. Const. Δέδωκεν 1. II. Stoic word for ἐπίρρημα II, Charis. p. 190 K.
ον, knavish like Pandeletus (cf. Cratin. 242), γνῶμαι Ar. Nu. 924, cf. Sch. ad loc.
ου, ὁ, = πανδερκής II, Ζεῦ π. βροτῶν E. El. 1177 (lyr.).

ές, seen by all, B. 16.70.
II. Act., all-seeing, AP 9.525.17, QS. 2.443, Orph. Fr. 62.
ου, ὁ, secure fastener, prob. name of a knot, δήσας τινὰ πανδέτην PMagLeid. V. 5.23.
ές, all-receiving, Pl. Ti. 51a ; ἀήρ Ph. 1.386 ; σῶμα Ocell. 2.3 ; φύσις Plu. 2.1014d ; μήτηρ ἁπάντων Orph. Fr. 315.3.

or πανδημί, Dor. πανδαμεί or πανδαμί A. Th. 296, Eu. 1038 (both lyr.) ; — Adv. of πάνδημος, with the whole people, in a mass or body, Hdt. 6.63, 7.120, al. ; π. προπέμπεσθαι ἐπὶ θάνατον Isoc. 10.27 ; π., πανομιλεί A. Th. l.c., cf. Eu. l.c. ; π. θύειν Th. 1.126 ; στρατεῦσαι Id. 5.33, cf. 1.73, 90, 4.42, Pl. Lg. 814a ; παρεῖναι And. 3.18 ; ἐξελθεῖν Lys. 2.49 ; τὸν βάρβαρον π. δέκεσθαι Hdt. 7.144, cf. 6.16, 8.40, 72. [-ι Trag. (nisi leg. -εί)· ι AP 5.43 (Rufin.) ; written -ί in IG 12(2).526 A 8, B 2 (Eresus, iv/iii BC), Ἀρχ. Δελτ. 9 παρ. 53 (ibid.) ; -εί in BGU 646.20 (ii AD).]
= πανδημεί.
ἡ, the whole people, π. ἐξάγειν Pl. Lg. 829b ; π. καθιστάναι, of Theseus in Attica, Arist. Fr. 384, Plu. Thes. 25 ; πανδημίᾳ, as Adv., = πανδημεί, A. Supp. 607.
ον, of or belonging to all the people, ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ πτωχὸς π. public beggar, Od. 18.1 ; π. ἄγρη a draught of all kinds of fish, AP 9.383.2.

Dor. πάνδαμος, ον, = πανδήμιος (esp. in Prose), βοῦς S. Aj. 175 (lyr.) ; ἀγών E. Alc. 1026 ; στέγαι Id. Ba. 227 ; π. πόλις, στρατός, the whole body of the city, of the army, S. Ant. 7, Aj. 844 ; π. χάρις general favour, Alcid. ap. Arist. Rh. 1406a26 ; δόξα Plb. 31.25.8 ; δεῖπνον IG 7.2712.79 (Acraeph.) ; ἀρχή Sammelb. 5765 (iii/iv AD) ; of diseases, pandemic, Gal. 17(1).2 ; epith. of Zeus at Athens, IG2². 1075. Adv. -μως, = πανδημεί, τοὺς ἀνθρώπους εὐώχησε π. ib. 5(2).268.43 (Mantinea). π. Ἔρως vulgar love, opp. οὐράνιος, Pl. Smp. 180e sq., cf. X. Smp. 8.9 ; π. Ἀφροδίτη Pl. Smp. 181a, IG2². 659, SIG 1014.57 (Erythrae, iii BC), Paus. 1.22.3, Luc. DMeretr. 7.1, etc. (also in pl., Dam. Pr. 97 bis) ; π. ἐρασταί Pl. Smp. 181e ; π. μουσική common, vulgar music, Aristox. Fr. Hist. 90 ; ἡ π. λέξις ordinary (common) speech, Phld. Rh. 1.165 S.
(sc. ἱερά), τά, a festival of Zeus at Athens, D. 21.9, IG2². 1172.9.

ον, all-righteous, φρήν S. Tr. 294 ; π. σέβας prob. in A. Supp. 776 (lyr.). Adv. -κως most justly, Id. Th. 172 (lyr.), 670, Ch. 241, S. OC 1306, E. Rh. 720 (lyr.) ; as in duty bound, S. Tr. 611, 1247.
ου, ὁ, son of Pandion, used of Pericles, Cratin. 56 (s.v.l.). fem. Πανδιονίς, ίδος, daughter of Pandion, χελίδων Sappho 88, cf. Hes. Op. 568. one of the Attic tribes, Aeschin. 2.169, Harp.
ον, all-divine, ῥίζα, = χελιδόνιον μέγα, Ps.-Dsc. 2.180 (Wellm. Πανδίονος ῥ.) ; pecul. fem., πανδῖα Σελήνη Max. 146 ; Π. alone, Id. 123.
ἡ, hostess, Hdn. Gr. 1.248 ; — written πανδόκια, IG 14.24 (Syracuse).
ἡ, trade of an innkeeper, Pl. Lg. 918d, Poll. 7.16.

(πανδοκίον (sic) Hsch.), τό, inn, Ar. Ra. 550, D. 19.158, Aeschin. 2.97, IG2². 1638.30, Philippid. 25.2, Com.Adesp. 159, Plb. 2.15.5 ; — later πανδοχεῖον, Thphr. Lap. 53 codd., Aen.Tact. 10.10 codd., Str. 5.3.9, 12.8.17, etc., condemned by Phryn. 276.

έως, ὁ, one who receives all comers, innkeeper, Pl. Lg. 918b, Plb. 2.15.6, Arr. Epict. 1.24.14, Plu. 2.234e, etc. ; metaph, πάσης κακίας π. Pl. R. 580a ; π. ᾍδης Lyc. 655 ; — later πανδοχεύς, Ev. Luc. 10.35 ; of the δεκάς, all-containing, Pythag. ap. Procl. in Ti. 3.107 D. ; also Pythag. name for unity, Theol.Ar. 6.
εως, ἡ, = πανδοκεία, Pl. Lg. 842d (pl.).
οῦ, ὁ, = πανδοκεύς, BGU 1468.3 (iii/ii BC, pl.).
ἡ, hostess, Ar. Ra. 114, Pl. 426, Eup. 9, DC. 46.6 ; metaph, φάλαινα π. a sea-monster ready to take all in, Ar. V. 35.

(< πάνδοκος) entertain as a host or innkeeper, Timocr. 1.10, Hdt. 4.95, Pl. Lg. 918e ; abs., keep an inn or lodging-house, Thphr. Char. 6.5 ; — Pass., to be furnished with inns, ὅσα μέρη πανδοκεύεται κατὰ τὴν δίοδον DH. 4.53.
= πανδοκεύω, only metaph, take upon oneself, assume, ἅπαντα παιδείας ὄτλον A. Th. 18.
= πανδόκια.
ἡ, = πανδοκεύτρια, St.Byz. s.v. Καππαδοκία.

or πανδόκος, ον, (< δέχομαι) all-receiving, common to all, χέρσος, of Hades, A. Th. 860 ; of the sacred places at Elis and Delphi, Pi. O. 3.17, P. 8.61 ; π. ξενίαι Id. O. 4.17 ; π. ξενόστασις S. Fr. 274 ; c. gen., δόμοι π. ξένων A. Ch. 662.
ἡ, absolute fame, perfect glory, Pi. N. 1.11.
ὁ, = πανδοκεύς, gen. -δοκος MAMA 3.576, al. (Corycus) ; gen. -δοχος ib. 459 (ibid.) ; nom. sg. in Hsch.
ἡ, one who gives herself to all, of a harlot, Anacr. 156, Com.Adesp. 1352.
εως, ἡ, an unknown article of household equipment, PLond. 2.191.6 (ii AD, pl.).
ον, slave to all, AP 5.21 (Rufin.), Man. 4.602.

or πανδούρα, ἡ, three-stringed lute (prob. of Oriental origin), Poll. 4.60, Ath. 4.183f ; — also πάνδουρος, ὁ, Euph. (?) ap. Ath. 4.183f, MAMA 3.24 (Seleucia ad Calycadnum) (written φάνδουρος and used of the monochord by Nicom. Harm. 4) ; — Dim. πανδούριον, τό, Hsch. and Phot. s.v. πηκτίς ; — also πανδουρίς, ίδος, ἡ, Hsch., Gloss.
play the πανδοῦρα, Hist. Aug. Elag. 32.
τό, Dim. of πανδοῦρα.
ίδος, ἡ, Dim. of πανδοῦρα.
οῦ, ὁ, one who plays πανδοῦρα, Euph. Fr. Hist. 8, JRS 18.177 (Jerash).
ὁ, = πανδοῦρα.
v. πανδοκεῖον.
v. πανδοκεύς.
τό, temple of Pandrosos, daughter of Cecrops and Agraulos, IG1². 372.45, 171, al.
ον, allpowerful, Procl. Theol.Plat. 4.27, Gloss.
ἡ, fem. Adj. ruling over all, ἄνασσα Tab. Defix. Aud. 38.27 (Alexandria, iii AD).
ον, poet. for πανόδυρτος, all-plaintive, αὐδά A. Pers. 941 (lyr.) ; θρῆνοι E. Hec. 212 (lyr.) ; ἀηδών S. El. 1077 (lyr.).
ἡ, total setting of a star, AP 7.273 (Leon.), 395 (Marc. Arg.), 502 (Nicaen.).
ἡ, giver of all, epith. of Earth (cf. πάνδωρος), Ar. Av. 971, Ph. 1.32. Pass. as fem. pr. n., Pandora, i.e. the All-endowed (i.e. by the gods), Hes. Op. 81.
ον, allbounteous, epith. of Earth, Hom. Epigr. 7, Opp. C. 1.12 ; dispenser of all (whether good or ill), αἶσα B. Fr. 20.4 ; Ζεύς Cleanth. 1.32.
ἡ, giver of all, φύσις, Δημήτηρ, Orph. H. 10.16, 40.3.
Adv. with the whole nation, ἀπολέσθαι Str. 5.1.6 ; — also πανεθνί, LXX Wi. 19.8.
= πανεθνεί.
κεχορτασμένη, Hsch. ; cf. πανός.
ον, furnished with all sorts of food, QS. 1.88.
ον, capable of assuming all forms, Zos.Alch. p. 205.
ές, of every figure, of unity (as the base of all figurate numbers), Theol.Ar. 4.
ον, like in all points, Man. 2.494.

ον, = πανεικέλιος, Opp. C. 1.434 ; c. dat., γάλακτι π. ῥεύματα AP 9.699, cf. 12.156, Supp.Epigr. 2.423 (Macedonia) ; also c. gen., ἰχὼρ π. γάλακτος Orph. L. 203 ; neut. as Adv., Call. Aet. Oxy. 2079.31.

ον, = Πανικός ; πάνειον, τό, = πανικόν, panic, Aen.Tact. 27.1, al. (ὄνομα Πελοποννήσιον καὶ μάλιστα Ἀρκαδικόν, l.c.). Πανεῖον, τό, sanctuary of Pan, Str. 9.1.21, 17.1.10, CIG 4837 (Egypt). Πάνεια, τά, festival of Pan at Delos, Inscr.Délos 312.6, 320 B 58 (iii BC).
ἀναιδής, Hsch.
ον, gen. ονος, all-merciful, Θεός Mitteis Chr. 361.8 (iv AD).
ον, entirely free, APl. 5.338, IG 14.400 (Lipara).

οἱ, all the Hellenes, Il. 2.530, Hes. Op. 528, Archil. 52, Str. 8.6.6, Ph. 2.477 ; τὸν Πανελλήνων νόμον σῴζων E. Supp. 526 ; οἱ Π. the Greeks, Phld. Mus. p. 78 K., Piet. 17, Rh. 2.224 S.
II. League of United Greeks formed by Hadrian, IG 7.2712.40, etc. ; also in sg., as title of a Councillor of the League, ib. 5(1).45, al.
άδος, ἡ, celebration of the Πανελλήνια (cf. Πανελλήνιος III), Supp.Epigr. 2.410 (Thessalonica, iii AD).

Ζεύς, ὁ, the chief god of the Πανέλληνες II, Paus. 1.18.9, 1.44.9, 2.29.8 ; also ἀγὼν Π. his festival, IG2². 1077.14 ; cf. III. II. Πανελλήνιον, τό, his temple, at Aegina, built by Hadrian as their meeting-place, Paus. 2.30.4, DC. 69.16.
body of Πανέλληνες II ; τὸ κοινὸν τοῦ Π. CIG 3832, cf. 3834.
III. τὰ Πανελλήνια the festival of the United Greeks, IG2². 1106, Philostr. VS 2.1.5, 2.17, etc.
ὁ, Dor. and Aeol. for πηνέλοψ, Alc. 84, Ibyc. 8.
v. Πάναμος.
ές, absolutely like, Tz. H. 8.419.
ον, allglorious, as title of address, PMasp. 2 iii 24 (vi AD).
ον, quite different, Hsch.
ον, far above, Orph. A. 81, Opp. C. 1.477 ; πάντων π. Man. 2.30 ; ἐν μούσαισι π. eminent in poetry, IG 12(8).442.3 (Thasos). Adv. -ως pre-eminently, PMasp. 2 i 1 (vi AD).
keep high festival, Puchstein Epigr.Gr. p. 61 (Egypt).
ον, kept as a high festival, Ph. 2.477.
ον, all-sufficient, Epigr. ap. Suid. s.v. Παλαμήδης.
ἡ, perfect loveliness, Eust. 1598.5.
ον, giving ear to all, θεός MAMA 1.8 (Laodicea Combusta).
ον, all-lovely, Χαρίτων εἶδος IG 14.1858.
ον, of very close texture ; neut. pl. as Adv., π. χευαμένοιο, of snow, falling thickly, Opp. C. 3.172.
ον, all-treacherous, Opp. C. 2.28.
ον, all-surveying, AP 7.245 (Gaet.), MAMA 1.171 (Laodicea Combusta).
ον, gen. ονος, all-knowing, Gal. 16.324, Sch. Pl. Phdr. 261d.
ον, gen. ονος, all-remarking ; πανεπίφρονα cunning arts, Opp. C. 1.328.
ου, ὁ, all-observing, LXX 2 Ma. 9.5 (v.l. παντεπ-), Dioscorus in PLit. Lond. 98 ii 11, PLond. 5.1676.65 (vi AD).
ον, (< ἐπί, ὄρφνη) all night long, AP 5.205 (Leon., s.v.l.).
ον, all-observing, Hermes 66.327 (Egypt), Nonn. D. 9.133, 32.94.
ου, ὁ, = πανεπόπτης, Ath.Mitt. 24.358 (Mytil.).
ου, ὁ, all-effecting, Ζεύς A. Ag. 1486 (lyr.).
ον, all-desolate, Str. 17.1.27, Heb. Je. 2.24, PFlor. 36.12 (iv AD), Luc. DMort. 27.2 πανέρως, έρωτος, ὁ, gem supposed to remove sterility, Plin. HN 37.178.
ον, lasting the whole evening, AP 7.194 (Mnasalc.).
ον, (< ἑστία) with all the household, Plu. Sol. 24.
ον, last of all, ARh. 4.308.
Adv., (< ἔτος) all the year long, Pi. P. 1.20.
ον, all-true, Orph. A. 540.
ον, all-ineffectual, Orph. A. 1228.
ές, most noble, Tz. H. 1.198 ; Sup., ib. 190.

ον, gen. ονος, quite happy, J. AJ 8.1.1, Plu. 2.1063d, Luc. Cont. 14.
all-blessed, as honorary title, βασιλεία OGI 722.2 (iv AD) ; πόλις (Constantinople) PMasp. 32.93 (vi AD).
ον, quite easy of access, χερρόνησος Plb. 4.56.6.
ον, all-silent, αἰθήρ ARh. 3.1196.
ον, very clever, Tz. H. 9.530.
ον, most beautiful, Tz. H. 2.17, 8.995 (both Sup.).
ές, all-comely, v.l. in D.Chr. 11.153 ; Sup., Tz. H. 8.518.
ὁ, perh. the all-round champion of the ἔφηβοι, IG2². 2221.45.
ές, most holy, τὸ π. ὑμῶν κράτος (of the Emperor) PMasp. 19.1 (vi AD).
ές, very strong, Tz. H. 2.569.
ές, very cheap, vile, Suid. s.v. ἀγοραῖος νοῦς.
ον, very active, AP 7.425 (Antip.Sid.).
Ion. -ίη, ἡ, all good fortune, Epigr.Gr. 443.
in Pass., to be praised everywhere, τὸ ἐν πᾶσι πανευφημούμενον ὑμῶν ὕψος PMasp. 2 i 4 (vi AD).
ον, all-praiseworthy, as honorary title, POxy. 136.6 (vi AD), etc.
ον, gen. ονος, (εὐφρόνη) = πάννυχος, Cratin. 435.
ές, good-natured, Tz. H. 4.854 (Sup.).
(< Πάν) treat after the manner of Pan, π. γυναῖκας Heraclit. Incred. 25.
ον, gloss on πάνθοινος, Sch. Oppian. H. 2.221.
ον, quite boiled ; of metals, quite cleansed of dross, κασσίτερος Hes. Sc. 208.
ές, all-hostile ; all-hateful, Orph. H. 61.11 ; Sup. πανέχθιστος Lyc. 1057.
ὁ, or πανέχινον, τό, dub.sens., ἐν πανεχίνῳ (v.l. πάχει νώτῳ) τῆς ἀσπίδος αὐτοῦ LXX Jb. 15.26.
Adv. with all the youth, Tz. H. 7.995.
όνος, ὁ, ruler of all, Ph. 1.227.
celebrate a πανήγυρις, SIG 344.3 (Teos, iv BC).
to be president of a πανήγυρις, SIG 869.9 (Eleusis, ii AD), IG 3.716, etc. ; πανηγυριαρχήσαντα καὶ ἀγωνοθετήσαντα τῶν μεγάλων Παναθηναίων ib. 709.

Dor. and Aeol. παναγυριάρχας, ου, ὁ, president of a πανήγυρις, Plu. 2.679b, IG 5(1).38 (Sparta), SIG 867.59 (Ephes., ii AD), IG 12(2).244, al. (Mytil.) ; — also πανηγυρίαρχος, ὁ, ib. 241 (Mytil.), Ephes. 3No. 14.
ὁ, = πανηγυριάρχης.

celebrate or attend a public festival, πανηγύριας π. keep holy-days, Hdt. 2.59 ; Ὀλύμπια καὶ Κάρνεια π. Plu. 2.873e ; τὴν τῶν ἐπινικίων ἡμέραν POxy. 705.35 (iii AD) ; abs., PSI 4.374.15 (iii BC) ; π. ἐς πόλιν go to a city to attend a festival, Hdn. 1.9.2 ; metaph, enjoy oneself, Alex. 219.17, Ael. VH 13.1.
frequent fairs or markets, App. Pun. 116. later, make a set speech in a public assembly, deliver a panegyric, Isoc. 5.13, Plu. 2.802e. Pass., sound as at a festival, of flutes, etc., Heraclit. All. 9.

ή, όν, of or for a public festival or assembly, οἱ ὄχλοι οἱ π. Isoc. 12.263 ; πολυτέλεια, κόσμος, Plu. 2.608f. generally, solemn, festive, λόγος festival oration, such as those pronounced at the Olympic games, panegyric, Isoc. 5.9, 84, al. ; Ἰσοκράτης ἐν τῷ π. in his Panegyric, Arist. Rh. 1408b15 ; π. εἶδος [τῆς ῥητορικῆς] Phld. Rh. 2.251 S. ; τὰ π. Plu. 2.79b ; Comp. -ώτερος, of Isocrates himself, DH. Vett. Cens. 5.2 ; πανηγυρικώτεραι διηγήσεις Aps. p. 257 H.
flattering, false, π. λῆροι Plu. 2.6a ; of style, showy, ostentatious, opp. ἀληθινός, DH. Dem. 8 ; of persons, pompous, γυνὴ σοβαρὰ καὶ π. Plu. Luc. 6. Adv. -κῶς showily, π. κατεσκευασμένος Id. Cam. 16, cf. Ant. 61 ; opp. στρατιωτικῶς, Posidon. 36 J. ; Comp. -κώτερον Plb. 5.34.3.

Dor. πανάγυρις, εως, ἡ, (< πᾶς, ἄγυρις) general or national assembly, ἐν πανηγύρει βουλευσόμεσθα A. Ag. 845 ; esp. a festal assembly in honour of a national god, Δήμητρος ἁγνῆς καὶ Κόρης Archil. 120 ; Ζηνὸς ἀμφὶ πανάγυριν Pi. O. 9.96 ; πανηγύριας πανηγυρίζειν, ποιήσασθαι, to hold such festivals, keep holy-days, Hdt. 2.59, 58 ; συναγαγεῖν Isoc. 4.1 ; διαλύειν X. Cyr. 6.1.10 ; ἐς π. θεωρεῖν Ar. Pax 342 ; θεωρίαι ἐς τὰς ἐν τῇ Ἑλλάδι π. Decr. ap. D. 18.91 ; Ὀλυμπίαζε εἰς τὴν τῶν Ἑλλήνων π. ἐπανιών Pl. Hp. Mi. 363c ; in Caria, PCair. Zen. 341 (a) 11 (iii BC) ; in Egypt, PHib. 27.76 (iii BC), etc. ; ἐν ταῖς π. καὶ δείξεσι τῶν σοφιστῶν Phld. Rh. 2.256S. ; ἁμίλλαις ἱππικαῖς καὶ πανηγύρει προσκαθήμενος Jul. Or. 1.39c ; π. ἐμπορικόν τι πρᾶγμα Str. 10.5.4, cf. CIG 4474.35 (Baetocaece), Prisc. p. 277 D.
